nodes.title: OpenSoldat architecture synthesis (whole-engine)
nodes.description:
WHOLE-ENGINE ARCHITECTURE (synthesis of 13 subsystem maps)

OpenSoldat is a server-authoritative 2D shooter split across three compilation targets that share one body of simulation code: shared/ (the deterministic game logic and protocol), client/ (rendering, audio, input, menus), and server/ (the dedicated host, RCON, bans, lobby, scripting). CMake builds two executables (soldat, soldatserver) from the same ~52 shared .pas files plus side-specific units, switching behavior with {$IFDEF SERVER}/{$IFDEF CLIENT}/{$IFDEF SCRIPT}/{$IFDEF STEAM}/{$IFDEF ENABLE_FAE} compile flags. The world is held entirely in 1-indexed global fixed-size arrays in shared/Game.pas: Sprite[1..MAX_SPRITES=32], Bullet[1..MAX_BULLETS=300], Thing[1..MAX_THINGS=256], Spark[], plus a single TPolyMap (collision geometry + sector spatial grid) and the shared ParticleSystem instances (SpriteParts, BulletParts, thing/weapon skeletons). There is no entity object graph — subsystems cross-reference each other purely through these global arrays and a shared MainTickCounter.

The simulation is a fixed-timestep loop at GOALTICKS/DEFAULT_GOALTICKS=60 Hz (dt=1/60). Both sides run the identical mechanics in shared/mechanics/ (Sprites.pas, Control.pas, Bullets.pas, Things.pas, Sparks.pas) on top of the Verlet/Euler integrator in shared/Parts.pas. The difference is the driver and the authority split: the server (server/ServerLoop.pas AppOnIdle) advances ticks off wall-clock time (Number27Timing -> Ticktime delta), runs authoritative physics/collision/damage, and schedules outbound network sends; the client (client/ClientGame.pas) accumulates real frame time into FrameTiming.Accumulator, runs Trunc(Accumulator/dt) catch-up ticks of client/UpdateFrame.pas (with client-side prediction of the local sprite), then renders at FramePercent interpolation between the last two authoritative states. The server is the single source of truth for sprite position/health/weapons, bullets, things, scores and respawns; clients send only their own input (Keys16 bitmap), client-predicted bullets (seed+velocity), votes and chat, and reconcile to server snapshots.

Networking (shared/network/, ~20 units over GameNetworkingSockets) glues the two simulations together with hand-coded packed-record messages (no real protobuf schema; protobuf only lives inside GNS). The server broadcasts full/major sprite snapshots, sprite deltas, skeleton snapshots for ragdolls, thing snapshots, and a reliable ~6s heartbeat carrying the scoreboard; it validates client bullets against weapon stats and ad-hoc cheat heuristics, and optionally runs the Fae challenge-response anti-cheat before sprite creation. Cvars (shared/Cvar.pas + Command.pas) are the universal config substrate; CVAR_SYNC server cvars (notably sv_gravity, sv_realisticmode, weapon tuning) are serialized and pushed to clients so the shared mechanics stay deterministic across the wire. The dedicated server additionally layers PascalScript modding (server/scriptcore/, two parallel engines ScriptCore v1 and ScriptCore3) that hooks game events synchronously on the main thread and reads/writes the same global game state directly.

--- PER-TICK PIPELINE ---
Per server tick (ServerLoop.AppOnIdle -> UpdateFrame, confirmed in server/ServerLoop.pas): Number27Timing computes how many 60Hz ticks of wall-clock elapsed -> UDP.ProcessLoop drains inbound network (applies client input/bullets/votes/chat) -> RCON ProcessCommands -> then for each elapsed tick: increment ServerTickCounter/MainTickCounter -> ScrptDispatcher.OnClockTick (PascalScript) -> Steam manual callbacks -> flood/ping/knife counter resets -> ServerSyncCvars if CvarsNeedSyncing -> UpdateFrame, which does: (1) shift OldSpritePos history ring for lag-comp, (2) SpriteParts.DoEulerTimeStepFor(j) integrate each player's particle body, (3) Sprite[j].Update (Control input->Forces, gravity/friction, CheckMapCollision, animation+IK skeleton, weapon/reload/jetpack state, death/ragdoll), (4) Bullet[j].Update (ballistics, map/sprite/thing/collider collision, damage, ricochet/penetration, explosions, sparks), (5) BulletParts.DoEulerTimeStep, (6) Thing[j].Update (flag/kit/weapon/M2 physics, pickup detection, touchdown scoring, timeouts/respawn), (7) bonus spawning -> back in AppOnIdle: demo SaveNextFrame, then time-sliced network scheduling keyed off MainTickCounter mod N (sprite snapshot, major snapshot, skeleton snapshot, heartbeat, deltas, per-player ping/thing snapshot, Fae challenges, disconnect timeout checks). The client UpdateFrame is the same core (DoEulerTimeStepFor -> Sprite.Update -> Bullet.Update -> Spark.Update -> BulletParts.DoEulerTimeStep -> Thing.Update) but adds Spark updates, runs client prediction for the local sprite, and is followed by RenderFrame(Elapsed, FramePercent) which interpolates between the two latest states and composes layers (background -> map back polys -> sprites/bullets/particles -> mid props -> front polys -> front props -> HUD).

--- CROSS-CUTTING CONCERNS ---
- Global mutable world state: Sprite[]/Bullet[]/Thing[]/Spark[] fixed 1-indexed arrays plus the single PolyMap and ParticleSystem instances in Game.pas are read/written directly by mechanics, networking, AI, scripting, rendering and server infra. There is no encapsulation boundary; everything is implicitly coupled through these arrays.
- Determinism across client/server: the exact same shared/mechanics + Parts.pas integrator must produce identical results on both sides for prediction/reconciliation to work. Magic physics constants (GRAV~0.06, RKV=0.98 damping, SURFACECOEFX/Y friction, per-thing gravity 1.0-1.4x and damping 0.989-0.996) and the 60Hz tick are baked into this determinism.
- The 60Hz fixed timestep (DEFAULT_GOALTICKS/GOALTICKS) is assumed everywhere: physics damping tuning, per-frame TimeOut decrements in bullets/things, network scheduling (MainTickCounter mod 30/15/20/...), bot stuck detection (90/180 frame thresholds), demo frame cadence, and lag-comp lookback all implicitly mean 'ticks == 1/60s'.
- MainTickCounter / ServerTickCounter / ClientTickCount are the shared clock. Snapshot scheduling, timeouts, anti-cheat windows, and lag compensation all key off them, but there is no explicit clock-sync protocol between client and server (loose, jitter-sensitive).
- Cvar networking: CVAR_SYNC server cvars (sv_gravity, sv_realisticmode, sv_friendlyfire, weapon tuning) are pushed to clients so shared mechanics behave identically; changing a synced cvar mid-game must be serialized and applied before the next prediction tick or determinism breaks.
- The shared mechanics are conditionally compiled, not abstracted: {$IFDEF SERVER} vs {$IFDEF CLIENT} branches inside Sprites/Bullets/Things select authority-vs-prediction, sound, and validation. Behavior diverges subtly per side within one file.
- Hand-rolled binary serialization (packed records in shared/network + BitStream.pas) couples the wire protocol to exact Pascal struct field order and alignment; TGun field order is even deliberately scrambled 'to piss off gamehackers', tying network/save compatibility to memory layout.
- Map format and CRC integrity: the binary .PMS layout (TMapPolygon/TMapSector/spawns/colliders/waypoints) and a CRC32 over the file buffer are shared between client load, server collision authority, and client-vs-server map validation.

nodes.title: Coupling hotspots (rewrite blast-radius)
nodes.description:
TOP COUPLING HOTSPOTS — hardest things to untangle in a rewrite:

* Global entity arrays (Sprite[]/Bullet[]/Thing[]/Spark[]) + shared ParticleSystem
  Every subsystem (mechanics, networking, AI, scripting, rendering, server loop) reaches directly into these 1-indexed fixed-size globals. There is no entity abstraction, so the cubic cross-reference Sprites<->Bullets<->Things and the shared Parts physics buffers cannot be untangled without touching nearly the whole codebase at once.

* shared/Parts.pas Verlet/Euler integrator coupled to sprite skeleton + map collision
  Player feel, ragdolls, bullets, and things all run through the same particle/constraint solver. Sprite.Update interleaves animation-driven skeleton positioning, IK, gravity/friction, and in-place velocity modification during collision response (Velocity := Velocity - Perp). Animation, physics, and (on client) render code are fused, so the physics layer cannot be replaced independently without retuning every feel-critical constant.

* ServerLoop.AppOnIdle network scheduling tied to MainTickCounter mod magic numbers
  Authoritative simulation, demo recording, anti-cheat timing, flood/ping enforcement, disconnect detection, and 10+ distinct snapshot/delta/heartbeat sends are all interleaved in one procedure keyed off MainTickCounter mod N (30/15/20/59/4/...) with a player-count Adjust factor. Network cadence, tick rate, and game logic are inseparable here.

* Hand-coded packed-record network protocol + BitStream
  50+ TMsg_* record types are serialized by raw memory layout with a giant switch-on-MsgID dispatcher in Net.pas and per-unit handlers. Any struct reordering, new entity type, or array-size change breaks wire compatibility and demo playback simultaneously; there is no schema/versioning layer.

* PascalScript ScriptCore directly bound to global game state, two parallel engines
  Every Script* API wrapper imports Server/Game/Sprites/Bullets/Things globals and mutates them directly under a single dispatcher lock. v1 (ScriptCore) and v2 (ScriptCore3) are both live with separate compile/exec models. A crashed OnClockTick can stall all event processing or shut down the server. This is the published mod API surface that the community depends on.

* Weapon definitions (Weapons.pas) feeding bullets, network validation, scripting, and serialization
  Guns[1..23] with inconsistent enum-to-index mappings (COLT_NUM=0 vs COLT=11), scrambled TGun field order, normal vs realistic stat tables, and BulletStyle used both as a weapon property and a bullet-dispatch enum. Adding/changing a weapon ripples into Bullets.pas, Sparks.pas, Constants.pas, network cheat validation, and the script weapon API.

nodes.title: Rewrite risk ranking by subsystem
nodes.description:
SUBSYSTEM RISK RANKING for total rewrite:

[HIGH] Player physics & movement (Sprites/Parts/Control) — The feel-defining core. Verlet integration + animation-coupled skeleton + in-place collision response + dozens of hand-tuned magic constants, all 60Hz-dependent and identical on client/server for prediction. Any deviation is immediately felt by players and silently breaks reconciliation.
[HIGH] Networking (protocol, prediction, lag-comp) — Hand-coded packed-record protocol with no versioning, single 50+ case MsgID switch, loose clock sync, seed-based client bullet spread, and PingTicks lag compensation. Compatibility and determinism are both at stake, and bugs surface as desync/cheat-window regressions.
[HIGH] Bullets & weapons — Velocity-dependent collision can tunnel thin geometry, scattered penetration/ricochet/flame-recursion magic constants, scrambled TGun layout coupled to serialization, BulletStyle dual-purposed, and cheat validation tied to exact weapon stats. High blast radius across weapons/sparks/network/scripting.
[HIGH] Scripting / PascalScript modding — Public mod API with two parallel engines, direct global-state mutation under one lock, synchronous main-thread dispatch where a crashed handler can stall the server. Hard to reproduce semantics in a new language while keeping the community's scripts working.
[HIGH] Game loop & core global state — Global 1-indexed fixed-size arrays and shared ParticleSystem are the foundation everything else couples to; the client/server tick drivers differ slightly. Reworking this touches the entire engine and underpins all other subsystems' risk.
[MEDIUM] Map system (PolyMap / .PMS / waypoints) — Binary format + CRC + sector math must stay load-compatible to keep the map library and server validation, but the collision query API is well-bounded and replaceable behind an interface; risk is mostly fidelity of format parsing and normal/bounciness decoding.
[MEDIUM] Things / map objects — Hardcoded per-type skeletons, gravity/damping, and game-mode logic (CTF/INF touchdown) baked into Update, plus inline networking. Coupled to sprites and protocol but a contained, mode-aware subsystem rather than a foundational one.
[MEDIUM] Server infrastructure (loop, bans, RCON, lobby, file server) — Heavy global state and blocking-socket/file-I/O patterns and magic tick scheduling, but largely orthogonal to gameplay feel; can be re-architected (async, indexed bans, command registry) without affecting determinism if the tick contract is preserved.
[MEDIUM] AI / bots — Monolithic ~600-line ControlBot mixing perception/decision/action, manual waypoint authoring tied to map layouts, and frame-count-based heuristics. Behavior is server-only and feeds the same Control path as humans, so it is replaceable but must keep waypoint format and produce believable play; getting bot feel right is non-trivial.
[MEDIUM] Config / Cvar / Command / Console — Universal substrate that gates rendering, networking sync, and scripting. CVAR_SYNC semantics are determinism-relevant, and globals are scattered across Server.pas/Client.pas, but the model itself is straightforward to reimplement with a typed registry.
[MEDIUM] Client rendering (OpenGL) — Large surface (Gfx/GameRendering/MapGraphics/Gostek/Interface) with fixed-pipeline fallback, bespoke batching, and skeleton-index/texture-ID coupling to gfx.inc. Client-local and interpolation-only, so it can be rebuilt on a modern renderer without protocol risk, but it is a lot of bespoke code to reproduce faithfully (skeleton layering, interface .sint compat).
[LOW] Client audio / input / menus — Client-local, well-isolated (SDL2 input, OpenAL spatial audio, menu widgets). Index-based sample table and absolute-coordinate menus are tedious but low-blast-radius; no determinism or protocol coupling beyond packaging input into messages.
[LOW] Build system & dependencies — CMake + FPC detection, pinned native libs, asset download. Mechanical to replace for a new toolchain and does not constrain runtime behavior, though dependency version pinning and FFI assumptions need attention during migration.

nodes.title: Rewrite considerations & next steps
nodes.description:
STRATEGIC REWRITE CONSIDERATIONS (what to preserve / decide early):

- Preserve movement feel bit-for-feel: the iconic Soldat physics lives in the Verlet integrator (Parts.pas) + Sprites/Control tuning (GRAV~0.06, RKV=0.98, SURFACECOEFX/Y, jump/jet impulses, polygon friction/ice/bouncy response). A modern physics engine (Rapier/Box2D) will not reproduce this without porting the exact integration and constants; consider porting the integrator verbatim first and only swapping it later behind an interface.
- Decide early whether the new client must stay net-compatible with existing servers (and vice versa). If yes, the hand-coded packed-record protocol, Keys16 input bitmap, snapshot/delta/heartbeat cadence, seed-based client bullet spread, and lag-comp (OldSpritePos ring, PingTicks lookback) must be reproduced byte-exact. If a clean break is acceptable, define a versioned schema (real protobuf/flatbuffers) but plan for a flag-day where old and new clients cannot mix.
- .PMS map format and CRC32 must be read bit-compatibly to keep the entire existing map library and client/server map-match validation working. The polygon normal-encodes bounciness in vector length, sectors are fixed per-map, and POLY_TYPE_* values (0-25) plus team collision flags are hardcoded — preserve these on load even if internal representation changes.
- The PascalScript mod API (ScriptCore/ScriptCore3 event names, signatures, and the Game/Map/Players/Bullets object model) is a public contract for server admins. A rewrite must either embed a Pascal-compatible scripting layer or provide a compatibility shim/transpile path, and must keep event dispatch order and damage-modifier cascade semantics, which scripts implicitly depend on.
- Lock the simulation to deterministic fixed 60Hz and keep all gameplay constants identical at launch. Determinism between predicting client and authoritative server is load-bearing; do not 'modernize' to variable timestep or float-different math until prediction/reconciliation is proven equivalent.
- Replace global fixed-size arrays with collections carefully: MAX_SPRITES=32 / MAX_BULLETS=300 / MAX_THINGS=256 and 1-indexing are encoded into the protocol, demo format, and script API (sentinel SpriteNum=0 = 'not joined'). Index 0 as sentinel and the hard caps cannot be silently changed without protocol/script breakage.
- Language/engine tradeoffs: Pascal-isms (Move() bulk array copies in Parts.pas, pointer arithmetic in BitStream, object-not-class value semantics, conditional compilation for client/server) map awkwardly to ECS/managed languages. An ECS rewrite is attractive but the cross-referencing Sprite<->Bullet<->Thing collision/damage code and animation-coupled skeleton will need a deliberate component decomposition, not a mechanical port.
- Keep demo format compatibility as an explicit decision: demos store raw network snapshots, so they are tied to both the tick rate and the wire layout. Either commit to replaying legacy demos (freeze the format) or accept dropping them.
- Anti-cheat (Fae) is optional and compile-gated; the fallback path is unencrypted. A rewrite should decide whether to keep Fae's challenge-response handshake (and its pre-sprite-creation gating) or design a replacement, but the bullet validation heuristics (speed/distance/timing/ammo) should be kept or upgraded to server-side replay to avoid regressing cheat resistance.

--- RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS to de-risk before committing to an approach ---
- Extract a written, authoritative spec of one full server tick and one client tick directly from server/ServerLoop.pas (AppOnIdle+UpdateFrame) and client/ClientGame.pas + client/UpdateFrame.pas, including the exact order, the MainTickCounter-mod network schedule, and where OnClockTick/demo/anti-cheat hook in. This is the behavioral contract a rewrite must match.
- Build a golden-master determinism test before rewriting: record a server-authoritative game (inputs + RNG seeds) and replay it, asserting bit-identical sprite/bullet/thing trajectories. Use it to validate any physics or integrator port against the original Parts.pas/Sprites.pas math.
- Inventory and freeze the wire protocol: enumerate all TMsg_* records, their field order/sizes, the MsgID switch in Net.pas, and the snapshot/delta/heartbeat cadence + Adjust factor. Decide explicitly whether the rewrite is net-compatible or a flag-day break, and document the lag-comp model (OldSpritePos ring, PingTicks, client bullet seed).
- Catalog the magic-constant surface that defines feel and balance: GRAV, RKV, SURFACECOEFX/Y, per-thing gravity/damping, bullet penetration/ricochet/degradation thresholds, weapon stat tables (normal + realistic), and distance/difficulty constants in AI. Centralize them into data so the rewrite can load and tune them identically.
- Specify the .PMS format and CRC32 from MapFile.pas/PolyMap.pas (polygon/sector/spawn/collider/waypoint layout, normal-length bounciness encoding, POLY_TYPE_* values) and write a round-trip loader/validator to guarantee the existing map library and client/server map matching keep working.
- Map the PascalScript public API: dump all ScriptDispatcher event signatures and the Script* object model (Game/Map/Players/Bullets/Weapons), plus event ordering and damage-cascade semantics. Decide the compatibility strategy (embed Pascal scripting vs shim/transpile) early, since it constrains the host-state architecture.
- Prototype the global-array-to-collection migration on one subsystem (e.g. Things) behind the existing index-based API to learn the cost of decoupling Sprite<->Bullet<->Thing cross-references and the 1-indexed/sentinel-0 assumptions before committing to an ECS or other model.

nodes.title: [game-loop] Game loop & core state
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: OpenSoldat is a FreePascal-based 2D multiplayer shooter with server-authoritative gameplay. This subsystem encompasses the fixed-timestep game simulation tick, main loop architecture (which differs between client and server), and the global game world state holding sprites, bullets, things, and map data. Both client and server maintain synchronized state through network snapshots and delta updates.

CLIENT/SERVER: AUTHORITY: Server is authoritative on all simulation (sprite positions, bullets, kills, map state). Client predicts own sprite movement but server corrects via position snapshots. NETWORK: Server sends sprite snapshots (full or major-change delta) at 30 ticks/sec (LAN) or configurable Hz (Internet via net_t1_snapshot/net_t1_delta CVars). Client sends input (control state) and position snapshots for cheat detection. Both maintain MainTickCounter synchronized. RENDERING: Client only. Server performs physics/game logic only. TICK RATE: Both use same GOALTICKS=60 (ticks/sec); dt = 1/60. Server drives tick via wall-clock time; client via combination of wall-clock and network heartbeat reception. DEAD RECKONING: Client extrapolates sprite positions between server snapshots using velocity; server sends skeleton (body bone positions) separately for corpses."

KEY TYPES: ParticleSystem = Verlet/Euler physics integrator storing NUM_PARTICLES (560) particles with position, velocity, forces, constraints for sprite skeleton animation; TSprite = Player character: holds Active, Health, Position (via Skeleton:ParticleSystem), Velocity, Control input, Weapon state, Animation state (LegsAnimation/BodyAnimation), direction, bonuses, teams; TBullet = Projectile: Active, Style (weapon type), Owner (sprite#), TimeOut counter, position/velocity via particle system; TThing = Collectible/Flag: Active, Style (OBJECT_* constant), Owner, HoldingSprite, Timeout, InBase, collision tracking; TSpark = Visual effect (client-only): Active, Life counter, Style, Owner, collision tracking; TPolyMap = Map geometry: PolyCount polygons, Sectors grid (spatial hash), Spawnpoints, Colliders, polygon types (deadly/ice/bouncy/etc), bounciness coefficients; TControl = Player input snapshot: Left/Right/Up/Down/Fire/Jetpack/ThrowNade booleans, MouseAimX/Y/MouseDist; TBotData = AI state: target, waypoint navigation, weapon preference, chat messages, accuracy, camping timer

RESPONSIBILITIES: Run fixed-timestep simulation at 60 ticks/sec (DEFAULT_GOALTICKS=60, SECOND=60 ticks); Accumulate variable frame time into fixed tick bucket and execute 1+ ticks per frame; Update sprite positions/velocities via ParticleSystem physics (Euler/Verlet integration); Update bullet trajectories and check collision with sprites/map/things; Update thing (flag/pickup) state, ownership, timeouts; Apply gravity, velocity damping, constraint satisfaction per physics tick; Send network snapshots of sprite state from server to client at configurable intervals (LAN vs Internet rates); Receive and apply client input snapshots and sprite position updates; Sync bullet fires, kills, flag captures, damage events across network; Manage demo recording by saving player positions and frame state; Handle map changes with countdown timer and scoreboard display; Manage game voting (map/kick) with time limits; Update game statistics, time limits, bonus spawning

DATA FLOW: CLIENT TICK LOOP (GameLoop in ClientGame.pas): 1. GetCurrentTime() measures SDL performance counter. 2. Calculate FrameTime delta since last frame. 3. Add FrameTime to Accumulator; extract complete ticks: TickTime += Trunc(Accumulator / dt) where dt = 1/GOALTICKS. 4. For each tick extracted: Inc(Ticks), Inc(ClientTickCount), Inc(MainTickCounter). 5. Call Update_Frame() [client per-tick update]: for j in Sprites: Sprite[j].Update(); for j in Bullets: Bullet[j].Update(); for j in Things: Thing[j].Update(); SparksUpdate. 6. Send ClientSpriteSnapshot (movement data) to server on MainTickCounter mod 7/5 (Internet/LAN). 7. Render happens decoupled: if (CurrentTime - PrevRenderTime) >= MinDeltaTime, call RenderFrame(FramePercent) where FramePercent interpolates between ticks.| SERVER TICK LOOP (AppOnIdle in ServerLoop.pas): 1. Number27Timing() updates system time; Timepassed accumulates. 2. UDP.ProcessLoop() drains network messages. 3. For MainControl := 1 to (TickTime - TickTimeLast): 4. Inc(Ticks), Inc(MainTickCounter), Inc(ServerTickCounter). 5. Call UpdateFrame() [server per-tick]: store OldSpritePos for all sprites, for j in Sprites: SpriteParts.DoEulerTimeStepFor(j) [physics], for j in Sprites: Sprite[j].Update() [gameplay]. 6. for j in Bullets: Bullet[j].Update(). 7. for j in Things: Thing[j].Update(). 8. Bonus spawn logic if not survival/realistic. 9. Network sending: ServerSpriteSnapshot (full state) mod 30 ticks (LAN) or net_t1_snapshot CVars (Internet). 10. ServerSpriteSnapshotMajor mod 15 (LAN) for major changes. 11. ServerSkeletonSnapshot mod 20 (dead body skeleton). 12. Ping per-player. 13. Map change counter decrements, triggers ChangeMap()."

INTERNAL DEPS: Sprites: owns TSprite array, depends on Weapons (gun state), Anims (animation playback), ParticleSystem (skeleton physics); Bullets: depends on Sprites (owner/hit detection), Things (collision); Things: depends on Sprites (held-by reference), Map (spawn points), physics via ParticleSystem; Parts (ParticleSystem): implements physics integration (Verlet/Euler), constraint satisfaction; PolyMap: stores map geometry, sector grid for spatial queries, spawn/collider data; Game: aggregates all world state (global arrays), tick counters, voting state; depends on Sprites/Bullets/Things/PolyMap; ServerLoop: depends on Game/Server/Sprites for UpdateFrame logic; calls UDP.ProcessLoop for network I/O; ClientGame: depends on Game/UpdateFrame/NetworkClientSprite for state updates; calls RenderFrame for graphics; Demo: depends on Game/Sprites for frame serialization

EXTERNAL DEPS: SDL2 (for GetPerformanceCounter/Frequency timing on client), GameNetworkingSockets (UDP wrapper for server-client messaging), PhysFS (file I/O for map/asset loading)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Fixed tick rate (60 Hz) hardcoded in DEFAULT_GOALTICKS constant; changing would cascade through timing calculations, network protocols, demo format
  - Global arrays (Sprite[1..MAX_SPRITES], Bullet[1..MAX_BULLETS], Thing[1..MAX_THINGS]) bypass object-oriented encapsulation; modernizing to dynamic collections would require protocol refactor
  - ParticleSystem uses fixed-size arrays (NUM_PARTICLES=560) and Verlet integration with magic damping constants (RKV=0.98) that couple physics behavior to tick rate
  - Frame-rate-independent tick accumulation logic (Trunc(Accumulator/dt)) appears in both client and server with slightly different logic; centralization would improve maintainability
  - Demo format stores raw snapshots; changing it breaks backward compatibility with recorded demos
  - Network snapshot scheduling uses MainTickCounter mod magic numbers (30, 15, 20); abstraction to configurable rates (CVars) exists but not consistently applied
  - Physics integrator (Verlet) is tightly coupled to sprite skeleton; refactoring physics layer independently is risky
  - Cubic complexity: Sprites -> Bullets -> Things all cross-reference; server-side collision/damage code intermixes updates with network sends
  - Pascal object syntax (object, not class) means no vtable polymorphism; adding new entity types (e.g. destructibles) requires modifying the core loop
  - Number27Timing uses GetTickCount64 with manual millisecond-to-tick conversion; clock-skew bugs possible if system time jumps

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - Why does Game.pas declare OldSpritePos[1..MAX_SPRITES, 0..MAX_OLDPOS] storing up to 125 old positions per sprite? Is this for interpolation, lag compensation, or spectator rewinding?
  - ServerLoop.UpdateFrame preserves OldSpritePos before physics update but client UpdateFrame doesn't; what is the asymmetry for?
  - What triggers demo playback speed change (demo_speed CVar)? Does it multiply GOALTICKS or just skip snapshots?
  - ClientGame.GameLoop has FramePercent := Min(1, Max(0, Accumulator / dt)); how does this interpolation percentage feed into RenderFrame?
  - Why does server rebuild DemoRecorder as a sprite (MAX_SPRITES slot)? Is it to inject demo actions into normal game update loop?
  - TSprite.NextPush[0..MAX_PUSHTICK] stores push impulses; how are they replayed and why store 125 ticks worth?
  - What is the difference between ServerSpriteSnapshot (interval=30) and ServerSpriteSnapshotMajor (interval=15)? Only on alternating ticks?
  - Network packet rate adjusts Adjust multiplier (0.66–1.0) based on HeavySendersNum; does this skip ticks or compress snapshots?
  - Why does the server track sprite.BulletCheck array and BulletCheckIndex? Is this anti-wallhack or anti-duplication detection?
  - Client has ClientStopMovingCounter used to freeze prediction; when does it reset and what triggers it?

nodes.title: [player-physics] Player physics & movement (Sprites/Control)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The Soldat movement system is built around a hybrid particle-constraint physics engine combined with direct animation-based skeletal positioning. The player (TSprite) maintains both a physics-integrated center-of-mass position (SpriteParts) and a constraint-based skeleton (ParticleSystem). Movement is driven by discrete directional impulses (Forces) applied each tick, with collision detection iteratively pushing the player away from polygon map boundaries. The skeleton remains kinematically pinned to the main body while providing ragdoll physics only after death.

CLIENT/SERVER: Shared code (shared/mechanics/Sprites.pas, Control.pas, etc.) runs identically on both client and server, with conditional compilation flags ({$IFDEF SERVER}) for: (a) server performs authoritative physics, sends snapshots to clients; (b) client predicts locally, receives corrections via network. Both use identical control input -> Force translation. Client-only: sound effects, rendering. Server-only: weapon hit validation, kill/death logging, respawn management. Authority: server (authoritative position, velocity used as baseline for client prediction).

KEY TYPES: TSprite = Main player entity. Contains: SpriteParts/Skeleton ParticleSystems, animations (legs/body), control input (TControl record), weapon state, health/vest/bonuses, collision flags (OnGround/OnGroundPermanent), physics-linked to map collision; ParticleSystem = Verlet integrator. Each particle has Pos, OldPos, Velocity, Forces, OneOverMass. Constraints link pairs with fixed rest-lengths. Used for both SpriteParts (player body center) and Skeleton (ragdoll limbs); TControl = Input state: Left/Right/Up/Down, Fire/Jetpack/Reload, MouseAimX/Y. Updated from input handlers, drives Force application; TAnimation = Frame-based skeletal data: 40 max frames, each with 20 joint positions. DoAnimation increments frame counter, positions applied to Skeleton particles during Update; Constraint = Linked pair of skeleton particles with fixed rest-length. Satisfied each Verlet step to maintain skeleton rigidity

RESPONSIBILITIES: Accept input (keyboard/mouse) and map to directional Forces (via ControlSprite in Control.pas); Integrate physics: Verlet stepping on SpriteParts.Velocity and SpriteParts.Pos each frame; Apply gravity (GRAV ~0.06) and apply friction to sliding (SURFACECOEFX/Y coefficients); Detect and resolve collision with polygon map: CheckMapCollision, CheckRadiusMapCollision, CheckMapVerticesCollision; Maintain ground state (OnGround flag) to gate jump availability and reduce friction on slopes; Animate skeleton: apply animation frame positions relative to body center, with head/arms IK-rotated toward aim target; Update Skeleton particles for ragdoll during death: full Verlet physics with broken constraints; Handle stance transitions (stand/crouch/prone) which affect animation and collision box position; Apply jetpack thrust (JETSPEED impulses, consume jet fuel counter); Weapon firing and reload state management

DATA FLOW: Each tick in TSprite.Update (line 438 in Sprites.pas): (1) input via ControlSprite updates Forces[Num]; (2) Verlet integration on SpriteParts advances velocity/position (line 1315: DoVerletTimeStepFor for arm parts); (3) collision checks against map polys (CheckMapCollision at lines 820-862) push player out and zero perpendicular velocity component; (4) ground state updated based on collision (OnGround); (5) skeleton animated: animation frame positions applied relative to body (lines 569-590), IK on head/arms toward mouse aim (lines 596-702); (6) dead skeleton gets full Verlet step (line 1333: DoVerletTimeStep) with broken constraints; (7) velocity clamped to MAX_VELOCITY (11.0) at frame end (lines 1414-1421). Forces reset to zero after each Verlet step in Parts.Verlet (line 145). NextPush deque holds network-delivered impulses from other players (line 463-470).

INTERNAL DEPS: Map/PolyMap: collision geometry, polygon types (ice, bouncy, deadly, etc), sector spatial indexing; Weapons: weapon firing, ammo state, reload timing; Anims: all animation data and playback logic; Things: held objects (flags, parachute) which attach to skeleton; Bullets: ballistics for weapons, impact detection; Particles/Sparks: visual effects from movement/collision; Network: input from remote players, push/impulse delivery

EXTERNAL DEPS: Vector math (custom in-engine implementation), None of the major SDL2/OpenGL/OpenAL deps are in the physics layer itself, PhysFS: used only to load .poa animation and .po skeleton files

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Verlet integration with tight constraint satisfaction loop: numerically sensitive, reimplementing in modern physics engine (Rapier/Bevy/etc) would need careful tuning to match the exact feel
  - Animation-driven skeleton: limbs animated first (lines 569-590), then IK applied to head/arms (lines 596-702), tightly coupled with render code; decoupling animation from skeleton physics is non-trivial
  - Polygon collision: custom point-in-poly, perpendicular distance, sectoring; would need to be replaced with proper 2D physics colliders (Box2D/Rapier), but the friction coefficients and response tuning are game-critical
  - Global Forces array per player: modified from multiple places (Control, jetpack, etc.); moving to component-based ECS would require significant refactoring
  - Pascal-specific: Move() used to bulk-copy particle arrays (Parts.pas line 234), would need equivalent in target language
  - Magic constants everywhere: GRAV, surface friction, jump heights, movement speeds are tightly tuned for the iconic feel; any change breaks gameplay
  - Constraints broken by damage: manually deactivating constraints during death (Die() lines 1982-1987) instead of constraint graph; no proper ragdoll solver
  - Tight feedback loop: map collision response modifies velocity in-place during collision checks (line 2750: Velocity = Velocity - Perp); side-effects-heavy code
  - Network push list: NextPush deque (lines 167, 463-470) for replay-able impulse delivery from network; tricky to replicate in event-driven systems

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - Why is Verlet integration chosen over Euler? (Parts.pas has both DoEulerTimeStep and DoVerletTimeStep, but only Verlet used for players; comment on line 134 says 'Verlet integration'). Likely for stability.
  - What determines the magic numbers: VDamping=0.997 (Anims.pas line 371), RKV=0.98 (Parts.pas line 32)? Where does 1.06 * GRAV come from for skeleton gravity (line 370)?
  - How does OnGroundPermanent (line 874) differ from OnGround? Used to gate slope handling but logic is subtle.
  - Why are constraint rest-lengths recomputed from loaded .po files but not updated after skeleton damage? Do broken limbs ever rejoin?
  - Background poly logic (BGState.BackgroundTest) seems complex (lines 3127-3198); when is it used and what problem does it solve?
  - How is NextPush deque populated by network code? No visible push/impulse apply in Control.pas itself.
  - Collision response (line 2750: Velocity -= Perp) could tunnel through thin walls if velocity is high; is there sub-stepping?
  - Why multiply bullet gravity by 2.25 (Anims.pas line 379) but spark gravity by 1/1.4? Different object masses?

nodes.title: [bullets-weapons] Bullets & weapons
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: Manages weapon definitions, bullet spawning, ballistics simulation, collision detection with sprites/map, damage application, and visual effects. Supports multiple bullet styles (hitscan-like projectiles, grenades, arrows, rockets, flames) with distinct physics and interaction behaviors. Integrated with the Parts particle system for realistic 2D physics simulation including gravity, damping, and constraint solving.

CLIENT/SERVER: {"client_side": "Bullet.Render() for trails/animations; spark rendering with life-based sprite/alpha; bullet tracking camera control; screen recoil (CalculateRecoil); screen flash on hit (HitSpray); immediate spark creation for feedback; ClientSendBullet() for fire notification; ClientBulletSnapshot() reception for remote bullets", "server_side": "ServerCreateBullet() for authoritative spawn with DontCheat flag; all collision/damage calculations; ExplosionHit() damage and health updates; ServerBulletSnapshot() to spectators; weapon drop logic; health decrement authority", "shared": "CreateBullet() code path (Net flag controls sync); TBullet.Update() collision checks identical on both; CheckMapCollision/CheckSpriteCollision/CheckThingCollision/CheckColliderCollision run with same constants; Hit() effects triggered by collision"}

KEY TYPES: TGun = Weapon record: name, ammo capacity, fire interval/startup/reload times, bullet speed, hit multiplier, bullet style, fire mode, spread, recoil, push force, inherited velocity, body part modifiers (head/chest/legs), clip reload flag, texture IDs, bink (screen shake), no-collision flags for friendly/team/self/explosion.; TBullet = Active bullet object: position/velocity via BulletParts, style (plain/shotgun/grenade/arrow/flame/etc), owner/weapon, hit multiplier, timeout counter, ricochet count, sprite/thing collision tracking sets, hitscan tracking flag, body part hit info.; TSpark = Visual effect particle: position/velocity via SparkParts, style (blood/smoke/explosion/shells/debris, 73 types), owner, life counter, collision counter for triggering sounds/destruction.; ParticleSystem (Parts) = Physics state: arrays of Active/Pos/OldPos/Velocity/Forces for up to 560 particles; Gravity, damping (VDamping/EDamping); constraint system for rigid bodies via Verlet integration.; TThingCollision = Bullet-flag collision cooldown: ThingNum, CooldownEnd to prevent repeated push ticks in single frame.; TSpriteIndexes = Distance-sorted sprite indices array for bullet collision prioritization in CheckSpriteCollision.; HIT_TYPE constants = Collision result enum: WALL, BLOOD, EXPLODE, FRAGNADE, THING, CLUSTERNADE, CLUSTER, FLAK, BODYHIT, RICOCHET; triggers different visual/sound effects.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Define 23 weapon types with damage, fire rate, ammo, reload, speed, spread, recoil, body-part modifiers (head 1.1-1.2x, chest 0.95-1x, legs 0.6-0.85x); Load weapon stats in normal vs realistic mode via CreateNormalWeapons/CreateRealisticWeapons procedures; Spawn bullets inheriting shooter velocity with random spread, apply startup charge time; Per-frame bullet physics: gravity (2.25x server gravity), Verlet damping (RKV=0.98), force accumulation; Collision detection: map polygons via sector-based spatial grid, sprite body parts via line-circle, Things (flags) via radial collision, Colliders via line-circle; Ricochet: bounce off map with surface normal reflection, velocity attenuation (25/35 existing + 10/35 normal), 6-frame offset to prevent re-collision; Arrow physics: gravity drag, sticks to surface after ARROW_RESIST (280) timeout expires, loses gravity post-impact; Grenade physics: surface friction GRENADE_SURFACECOEF=0.880 (velocity *= 0.88 post-bounce), Euler integration; Damage application: Speed * HitMultiply * BodyPartModifier; distance-based degradation (50% at 500px, 75% at 900px); Projectile penetration: slow bullets stop on first hit; cadavers/high-speed bullets (Speed > 23 or Speed >= 0.9*WeaponSpeed) pierce and continue at reduced velocity (0.9x or 0.75x or 0.66x); Flame bullet recursion: bounces off live targets, creates new flame with 2/3 damage, max 2 ricochets; Explosion radius damage via ExplosionHit(): spawns fragmenting projectiles (cluster/LAW/M79), affects all nearby sprites; Spark generation: shell casings on fire, blood mist on body hit, puff on impact, clothes tearing, wall impact sparks, debris on collider; Special melee handling: knife/punch from owner hand position, different collision StartPoint calculation, continue to next sprite on hit; Hitscan-style weapons: shotgun (multi-pellet spread BulletSpread), flamethrower (continuous beam), punch/knife (close range melee)

DATA FLOW: ["Spawn: WeaponIndex lookup via WeaponNumToIndex -> BulletStyle -> CreateBullet(pos, vel, num, owner, style, hitMultiply, net=True/False) -> BulletParts.CreatePart() -> optional network sync if FireInterval > FIREINTERVAL_NET or MustCreate", "Update loop: (1) CheckOutOfBounds() -> kill if outside sector bounds (2) CheckMapCollision() with step-accuracy (vel / 2.5 steps) -> iterate sector polygons -> PointInPolyEdges test -> ricochet logic (D > 50px check) or kill (3) CheckColliderCollision() -> line-circle vs 128 colliders -> ignite or kill (4) CheckSpriteCollision() -> FilterSpritesByDistance -> iterate body parts -> line-circle collision -> damage + push to NextPush queue + Hit(HIT_TYPE_BLOOD/BODYHIT) (5) CheckThingCollision() -> flag push with cooldown tracking (6) TimeOut decrement -> auto-explode at 0 (7) Distance-based damage degrade at 500/900px (8) Gravity accumulation (flame: -0.15 Y-force, arrow: +0.06 drag offset)", "Damage: Speed * HitMultiply * BodyPartModifier -> Sprite.HealthHit(damage, owner, bodypart, bulletnum, norm) -> weapon drop on punch, health decrement, audio feedback", "Spark spawn: Hit() generates style-specific sparks -> CreateSpark(pos, vel, style, owner, lifetime) -> SparkParts.CreatePart() -> visual feedback queued", "Spark update: DoEulerTimeStepFor() or skip (non-Euler) -> CheckMapCollision() -> bounce with SPARK_SURFACECOEF=0.7 -> style-specific effects (shell sounds, ricochets, splats) -> Life decrement -> Kill at 0", "Rendering: Bullet trail-scaled sprite rotated to velocity angle; grenade spinning; arrow with smoke; M79 with smoke; flame as animation frame; spark as style-specific sprite/sequence."]

INTERNAL DEPS: Sprites: position, skeleton (body part positions), health, team, armor, velocity for collision; Map/PolyMap: polygon geometry with type flags, sector grid (~512px division), surface normal calculation, ray-casting for LOS in realistic mode; Parts: particle physics engine (Verlet/Euler integration, gravity, damping); shared container for all dynamic objects; Constants: timeouts, limits, bullet trail scale parameters, sprite/spark max counts; Sound: hit sounds, ricochet, explosion, impact audio at bullet position; Cvar: sv_gravity (gravity scaling), sv_friendlyfire (damage rules), sv_realisticmode (LOS checks), r_maxsparks (spark limits); Things: flag/objective physics for bullet push interaction; Network: ClientSendBullet/ServerBulletSnapshot for replication across clients; Game loop: MainTickCounter for timeout tracking, CameraFollowSprite for visibility culling

EXTERNAL DEPS: Vector math: Vec2Add, Vec2Subtract, Vec2Scale, Vec2Normalize, Vec2Dot, Vec2Length, SqrDist, Angle2Points, Line-circle collision: LineCircleCollision() for bullet-sprite and bullet-collider checks, Rendering: Gfx.GfxDrawSprite() with rotation/scale/alpha, texture array indexed by GFX_* constants, Sound: PlaySound() with position-based 3D falloff, Physics: Verlet integration in Parts.pas, gravity accumulation, Map format: PolyMap binary with POLY_TYPE enums, sector division grid

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Weapon array indexing: Guns[1..23] with scattered enum-to-index mappings (COLT_NUM=0 but COLT constant=11); inconsistent naming scheme breaks refactoring
  - Scrambled field order in TGun (comment 'to piss off gamehackers') couples Pascal serialization to specific layout; any reordering breaks compatibility
  - Magic constants: ricochet attenuation (25/35, 10/35), penetration thresholds (0.9, 0.75, 0.66), step accuracy (vel/2.5), surface friction (0.88, 0.7) scattered without centralization
  - Tight BulletStyle coupling: enum used as weapon property AND bullet dispatch; adding new type requires changes in weapons.pas, bullets.pas, sparks.pas, constants.pas
  - Ricochet safety heuristic: D > 50px check prevents immediate re-collision but is fragile; no formal state machine
  - Hardcoded damage degradation: 500px and 900px distances in Update() with no per-weapon tuning
  - Melee special-casing: knife/punch have different StartPoint calculation, collision logic, penetration rules scattered throughout CheckSpriteCollision
  - Arrow physics fragility: ARROW_RESIST=280 timeout, gravity toggle, Forces adjustment diverge from other projectiles with no abstraction
  - Flame recursion risk: RicochetCount < 2 check is hardcoded; removing limit could cause infinite recursion; damage scaling (2/3) undocumented
  - Realistic mode fragmentation: MovementAcc, Bink, Recoil scattered across CreateNormalWeapons/CreateRealisticWeapons with no clean mode abstraction
  - Collision tracking: SpriteCollisions set for melee prevents double-hits but relies on caller bookkeeping; no formal state machine
  - Network decisions split: FIREINTERVAL_NET threshold in Cvar.pas vs style checks in Bullets.pas; inconsistent ownership
  - TimeOut per-frame decrement: no abstraction for server tick rate; assumes 60 FPS implicitly
  - Collision accuracy dependent on velocity: LargestVelocityComponent/2.5 can miss thin obstacles if moving too fast

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - Where is weapon INI loading? TGun.IniName field exists but no loading code visible in Weapons.pas; likely in Server.pas or SharedConfig.pas
  - What does 'Bink' do? (Suspected screen shake amplitude; never found in code that uses it)
  - What is 'MovementAcc'? (Suspected recoil/aim shake; only set in weapon defs, never used in visible code)
  - How are grenades detonated if they don't explode on map collision? (Grenades bounce until TimeOut=0 unless hitting sprite; is this intentional?)
  - Arrow drag physics: ARROW_RESIST=280 is a timeout, but is there explicit air resistance or drag formula?
  - Distance degradation formula: is 500px/900px threshold global or per-weapon tunable?
  - Where is FireMode used? (0=auto, 1=?, 2=semi in TGun but never referenced in Bullets.pas)
  - StartUpTime (charge-up) stored but never checked in CreateBullet or Update; where is startup delay enforced?
  - Recoil field in TGun never found in code; is it client-side only or unimplemented?
  - Why is CanHitSpray wrapped in {$IFNDEF SERVER}? (Friendly fire handled differently on client vs server?)
  - ExplosionHit() implementation cut off; what is blast radius and damage falloff formula?
  - How does punch/knife determine melee range? (StartPoint calculated via ButtstockPositionOffset * 4, but what is that offset value in hand space?)

nodes.title: [things-objects] Things / map objects (flags, kits)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: Things are the interactive, physics-enabled world objects in OpenSoldat including CTF flags, weapons, and bonus kits. The system manages their spawning, physics updates, collision detection with players, and pickup/interaction mechanics. Things are critical to game modes like CTF where flags serve as objectives, and provide essential gameplay elements like weapons, healing, and power-ups scattered across maps.

CLIENT/SERVER: Authority: Server exclusively handles pickup detection (CheckSpriteCollision), spawn/respawn, timeout logic, and network updates via ServerThingTaken. Clients receive snapshots and simulate rendering/physics locally for display. Prediction: Clients interpolate Thing positions from skeleton pos/oldpos for smooth animation between snapshot updates. Flags/weapons handled with high-frequency snapshots (every tick if moving). Stationary guns managed entirely on server; client gets visual updates only."

KEY TYPES: TThing = Core object record storing physics state (skeleton with 4 particles for verlet integration), style enum, hold state, timeout, collision flags, rendering data, and interaction metadata; TThingCollision = Lightweight record caching cooldown state for thing pickup to prevent duplicate processing; ParticleSystem = Verlet physics engine cloned per Thing for gravity, damping, and skeletal constraints; TVector2 = 2D position/velocity vectors used throughout skeleton physics; TMapPolygon = Map geometry used for collision detection in CheckMapCollision

RESPONSIBILITIES: Create Things with ownership and spawning mechanics (flags appear in team spawn points, weapons inherit player velocity on drop, kits spawn at map spawn points); Simulate physics each tick using verlet integration with gravity, damping, and collision response; Detect collisions with map geometry, applying bounce/slide physics or stopping when static; Detect collisions with players via radius checks, triggering pickup logic based on Thing type and player state; Handle flag gameplay: check if in base, detect touchdown scoring, manage holding/dropping; Handle weapon pickups: apply weapon to player, set ammo count from Thing, check cooldowns; Handle bonus kit pickups: grant healing, grenades, special modes (Flamer God, Predator, Berserker), vests, cluster grenades; Handle stationary gun (M2) interaction: allow player to mount gun, manage overheat/aiming, fire bullets; Respawn Things: rebuild skeleton, reset timeouts, randomize spawn location by team; Manage timeouts: remove expired weapons and kits, respawn flags when timeout expired; Render visual representations: flags with cloth physics, weapons with rotation, parachute with rope/canopy, stationary guns with base/turret; Network synchronization: send Thing snapshots to clients, handle creation/pickup/respawn messages

DATA FLOW: On each tick: (1) Server loop calls Thing[j].Update() for all active things. (2) Update() checks map collisions and applies physics via Skeleton.DoVerletTimeStep(). (3) If not static and held by sprite, syncs position to sprite hand position. (4) Checks if flag in base radius or if touchdown detected (other flag in base + enemy holding). (5) On server, calls CheckSpriteCollision() to detect pickup collision and handle application (weapons, kits, flags). (6) Applies timeout countdown, triggers Respawn() or Kill() based on type and timeout. (7) NetworkServerThing sends Thing snapshots to all clients either every tick (if moving) or periodically (for flags). (8) Clients receive snapshots, update skeleton positions, call Thing.Update() for rendering. (9) When Thing picked up, ServerThingTaken() broadcasts pickup message to all clients via NET."

INTERNAL DEPS: Sprites: collision detection uses SpriteParts.Pos array and Sprite[].Health/.Weapon/.TertiaryWeapon state to check pickup conditions; PolyMap/Constants: collision detection vs map polygons, sector-based spatial partitioning, team-based collide flags; Bullets: weapons Things can collide with bullets if sv_guns_collide set; Anims: rendering uses player animation Change.ID to check if player mid-animation before pickup; NetworkServerThing: Thing snapshot messages, PlayerTaken messages; Sound: OnPickup uses PlaySound for weapon/kit/flag capture sounds; Sparks: rendering uses CreateSpark for visual effects on touchdown/pickup

EXTERNAL DEPS: Verlet physics engine: custom ParticleSystem with Force/Constraint-based simulation, no external physics lib

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Skeleton physics: 4-particle verlet system is tightly coupled to Thing creation (different skeletons per weapon type: RifleSkeleton10/11/22/etc); refactoring would require abstracting skeleton shapes
  - Magic constants: Gravity scales per object type (1.0 to 1.4 GRAV), damping per type (0.989 to 0.996), spawn velocities hardcoded in CreateThing; no data-driven config
  - Global arrays: Thing[1..MAX_THINGS] is global mutable state; tight coupling with Sprite array and networking
  - Hardcoded game mode logic: Flag touchdown, CTF team detection, Infiltration mode all baked into TThing.Update; would need refactor for new modes
  - Networking: ServerThingTaken called inline during pickup; if async/batched later, would break synchronicity
  - Pascal idioms: Heavy use of object methods, global Thing/Sprite arrays, conditional compilation (SERVER/CLIENT), old-style parameter passing

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How are Thing skeleton types (RifleSkeleton10, RifleSkeleton11, etc.) generated from weapon models? Are these pre-built or procedurally generated?
  - What determines the 4-particle structure of flag/weapon skeletons? Why not use variable particle counts for different shapes?
  - How does the verlet integration handle constraints (e.g., keeping weapon particle distances fixed)? Is there a constraint solver?
  - Why are pickup conditions scattered across many 'if' statements in CheckSpriteCollision instead of data-driven? (e.g., medical kit checks health < STARTHEALTH AND HasPack=False on server but not client)
  - How does the stationary gun (M2) track which player is using it? Sprite[].Stat field -- is this robust against disconnects?
  - What happens if a flag is held and the player drops out? Does the flag reset, or does it stay in limbo with HoldingSprite=0?
  - Why does the Rambo Bow destroy itself when any player with bow weapon number is found in Update()? Is this a respawn mechanism?

nodes.title: [map-system] Map system (PolyMap, waypoints)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The Soldat map system is a polygon-based collision geometry engine with a spatial acceleration structure (sectors) that organizes triangular collision polygons across a 2D world. It handles loading binary .PMS map files containing collision geometry, scenery, props, spawn points, and bot navigation waypoints, then renders the visuals while maintaining real-time collision detection for gameplay.

CLIENT/SERVER: Server uses PolyMap, MapFile, Waypoints for collision and pathfinding logic (physics authority). Client uses all four modules: MapFile for loading, PolyMap for collision, Waypoints for AI, and MapGraphics for rendering. Network sync of player positions validated against server-authoritative collisions; client predicts movement using local PolyMap copy."

KEY TYPES: TMapPolygon = Triangle collision polygon with 3 vertices, surface normals (per-edge), material type (PolyType), and texture index. Normals are stored as TVector3 and used for collision response.; TMapSector = Spatial grid cell containing a dynamic array of polygon indices (Word values). Sectors partition the world space to accelerate collision queries.; TMapSpawnpoint = Player spawn location with (x, y) position, team ID, and active flag. Teams 1-4 are player teams; teams 5-6 are flag spawns.; TMapCollider = Circular obstacle (x, y center, radius) used for raycast queries. Active flag controls whether it participates in tests.; TWaypoint = Bot navigation node with ID, (x, y) position, directional hints (Left/Right/Up/Down), jetpack flag, action (wait/camp), and connections array to other waypoints.; TPolyMap = Main collision map object storing polygons, sectors, spawnpoints, colliders, waypoints, and query functions. Loaded once per map and persists throughout gameplay.; TMapFile = In-memory representation of a parsed .PMS file. Contains all map data before it is transferred to TPolyMap and TMapGraphics.; TMapGraphics = Client-side GPU resources for rendering: vertex/index buffers, textures, animated props, edges, background quad, and minimap sprite.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Load and parse binary .PMS map files into memory structures (MapFile.pas); Organize collision polygons into sectors for O(1) spatial lookup (PolyMap.pas); Provide collision detection queries: point-in-polygon, line-in-polygon, raycasts (PolyMap.pas); Perform polygon normal-based collision response and obstacle avoidance (ClosestPerpendicular, CollisionTest functions); Load map textures and build GPU vertex/index buffers for rendering (MapGraphics.pas); Render polygon terrain, animated scenery props, and edges at correct depth layers (MapGraphics.pas); Generate and cache minimap sprite from map geometry (MapGraphics.pas); Store bot navigation waypoints with directional hints and inter-waypoint connections (Waypoints.pas); Validate spawn points and waypoints for out-of-bounds coordinates; Support team-specific collision rules (team-colored barriers, flagger-only areas)

DATA FLOW: Load phase: ReadAllBytes (disk/archive) → MapFile struct → TPolyMap.LoadData copies polygons/sectors/spawnpoints → BotPath.Waypoint copied. Query phase (per frame): Physics/AI calls RayCast/CollisionTest → hash position into sector → iterate sector's polygon list → PointInPoly test → ClosestPerpendicular for normal. Render phase: UpdateProps animates scenery → GfxUpdateBuffer writes UV coords → RenderProps draws indexed buffers per texture and depth level. Minimap phase: GfxTarget onto texture → render all polygons at world scale → downsample to display size.

INTERNAL DEPS: Util.pas (TMapInfo record); Vector.pas (TVector2, TVector3 math); Game.pas (BotPath global, MainConsole); Calc.pas (Distance, PointLineDistance functions); PhysFS.pas (file system abstraction)

EXTERNAL DEPS: PhysFS (virtual file system for map loading from archives), OpenGL/SDL2 (graphics via Gfx module for texture and buffer operations)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Pascal 1-indexed arrays (Polys[1..MAX_POLYS]) differ from modern 0-indexed languages; sector offset calculation and loops must be carefully preserved
  - Sector math uses float division and Round() which may lose precision or cause boundary issues if refactored
  - Polygon normal encoding: Normals[3] stores bounciness as vector length; must be decoded during load (line 204: Vec2Length(Perp[i][3]))
  - Magic constants: POLY_TYPE_* are hard-coded (0-25), team enum values hard-coded in RayCast conditions; no enum-driven abstraction
  - Point-in-polygon test uses undocumented 2D cross-product determinant logic; lacks reference documentation
  - CRC32 hash computed over entire file buffer for integrity (line 449); cryptographic assumptions not explicit
  - Sector divisions are fixed per-map; no dynamic spatial structure adaptation
  - Edge rendering only on client; server has no visual edge data, risks asymmetric visibility
  - Background polygon types (POLY_TYPE_BACKGROUND) have special rendering logic mixed with collision logic
  - Minimap supersampling (4x) hard-coded; no configuration or quality slider

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - What is the exact file format version? MapFile.Version is read (line 288) but never validated or documented.
  - Are there additional polygon types beyond 0-25? Can the PolyType enum be extended?
  - How are colliders (circular obstacles) used in bot pathfinding? RayCast checks them but TWaypoint doesn't reference them.
  - What do the Normals[1..3] TVector3 fields represent beyond edge normals? Z component never used in collision.
  - Why is bounciness encoded as the magnitude of Normals[3]? Can elasticity vary per-polygon or is it global?
  - Do sector boundaries cause collision artifacts at borders between grid cells?
  - How are team-colored barriers (POLY_TYPE_RED_PLAYER, etc.) handled in bot pathing? Do waypoints have team affinity?
  - What happens when a player crosses an invalid sector coordinate? Bounds checking seems to reject the query but allows out-of-bounds movement.
  - Are background polygons (layers 0 and 1) used for occlusion or purely visual depth ordering?
  - Why is there both a BackPolys pointer array and Polys array? What is the purpose of BackPolyCount?

nodes.title: [networking] Networking (protobuf / GameNetworkingSockets)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: OpenSoldat's networking layer manages all client-server communication, state synchronization, and game logic replication using Valve's GameNetworkingSockets (GNS) and protobuf-like binary message formats. It implements server-authoritative gameplay with client-side prediction for movement/bullets, delta compression for bandwidth efficiency, a challenge-response anti-cheat system (Fae), and both reliable/unreliable message channels for real-time multiplayer action.

CLIENT/SERVER: SERVER AUTHORITY:
  - All game logic execution: sprite physics, bullet collisions, damage, scoring, respawn timers
  - State of truth: sprite position/health/weapons; receives client inputs (bullets, movement) and validates
  - Cheat prevention: validates bullet speed, distance from hand, weapon switch timing, ammo consumption, grenade/knife spam
  - Broadcasts authoritative state to all clients via snapshots

CLIENT PREDICTION & LAG COMPENSATION:
  - Input prediction: Client applies own movement and weapon fire immediately (1-frame latency for user)
  - Bullet prediction: Client-side bullets use same spread math (seeded with BulletSnap.Seed) as server to match pellet spread
  - Render-side interpolation: Client lerps other player positions between snapshots using delta time and velocity
  - Ping compensation: ClientSpriteSnapshot_Mov timestamped with ClientTickCount; server computes PingTicksB (current tick - client tick); client bullet receiver loops N ticks (pa = Owner.PingTicks + MySprite.PingTicks) to fast-forward bullet to server time before rendering
  - Authority conflict resolution: When server snapshot arrives, client updates position/health to server truth; if large divergence, may indicate cheat or lag

ASYMMETRY:
  - Client sends: own position, bullets, inputs, votes, chat; no other sprites' states
  - Server sends: all sprites to all players, all bullets (unreliable), all things, scoreboard, map/mode changes, Fae challenges
  - Server can force state (ForcePosition, ForceVelocity, ForceWeapon) if client deviates too far
  - Only server creates authoritative bullets; client bullets are hints, server creates its own and broadcasts

KEY TYPES: TNetwork / TClientNetwork / TServerNetwork = Base class and subclasses wrapping Valve GNS: manages socket creation, connection events, message send/receive loop (ProcessLoop), stats; TPlayer = Player object attached to each GNS connection (server) or allocated statically (client); contains name, colors, team, kills/deaths, ping/connection quality, sprite reference, Fae challenge secret, encryption key, anti-flood counters; TMsgHeader / TMsg_* = Binary message packet formats (packed records): ~50+ message types including sprites, bullets, things, heartbeat, chat, votes, map change, Fae challenges, connection handshakes; TMsg_ServerSpriteSnapshot = Full sprite state (position, velocity, health, weapons, ammo, keys/controls, helmet state, aim direction); sent unreliable ~30Hz; TMsg_ServerSpriteDelta_* = Delta updates (movement, weapons, helmet, mouse aim) sent to visible players only; bandwidth optimization via visibility checks; TMsg_BulletSnapshot = Bullet creation: owner, weapon, position, velocity, seed (for client-side spread randomness), forced flag (server-created vs client-created); TMsg_ServerThingSnapshot / TMsg_ServerThingMustSnapshot = Thing (weapon/flag pickup) state: position, velocity (4 skeleton points), owner, holding sprite; MustSnapshot forces delivery via reliable channel; TMsg_HeartBeat = Periodic sync (every few seconds): team scores, per-player kills/deaths/ping/flags/team, map ID for consistency checking; TMsg_FaeChallenge / TMsg_FaeResponse = Anti-cheat attestation: challenge (secret + request) and response (signed attestation); InOrder flag indicates synchronous (before player join) vs async; TMsg_PlayersList = Initial game state on join: all active players, their colors/teams/positions/velocities, mod checksum, map checksum, server ticks, anti-cheat requirement flag

RESPONSIBILITIES: Transport: Establish TCP-like connections via GameNetworkingSockets (supports both Steam and standalone IP), handle connection state changes (Connecting, Connected, Closed); Handshake: Multi-stage join process (RequestGame → validate version/password/bans → ServerVars sync → PlayersList → PlayerInfo → NewPlayer sprite creation); State Replication: Server broadcasts sprite snapshots (full or major updates) at ~30 Hz, sends delta updates for weapons/movement/aim to visible players only, reliable heartbeats every ~6 seconds; Bullet Replication: Client sends bullets with seed + velocity for client-side spread regeneration; server validates against weapon properties and cheat patterns (speed, distance, ammo, timing); broadcasts to non-shooter players; Thing Replication: Server sends optional snapshots for moving things, forced (reliable) snapshots for critical objects (flags, weapons), thing-taken events; Lag Compensation: Client-side bullets timestamped with ClientTickCount; server calculates ping-based lookback (PingTicksB); client lerps server positions using ping offset (OwnerPingTick + MySprite.PingTicks); Client-Side Prediction: Client applies own movement/bullet firing locally without waiting for server confirmation; server snapshot corrects divergence; Input Encoding: Keys16 bitmap encodes all input (movement, fire, jetpack, grenade, reload, flag throw); sent in ClientSpriteSnapshot_Mov messages unreliably; Anti-Cheat (Fae): Challenge-response system using FaeRemoteAttestation; server sends challenge before player joins, client responds with signed attestation; invalid/tampered clients rejected before sprite creation; encrypted session established post-auth; Chat/Messages: Reliable delivery for chat, supports command/public/team/radio message types, server enforces chat flooding limits, muted player detection; Voting: Kick and map voting with UI, server relays votes, client sends vote kick/map requests; Demo Recording: Parallel recording of all network messages for playback; Flood Protection: Per-IP request rate tracking, chat message frequency limits, bullet spam detection, grenade spam detection, knife throw timing validation

DATA FLOW: On each game tick (60 Hz server, 60 Hz client):
SERVER TICK LOOP (Server.pas): 
  1. Physics step (sprite movement, bullet simulation, collisions)
  2. ServerSpriteSnapshot: For each active non-dead player, if state changed significantly, send full snapshot unreliable to all players
  3. ServerSpriteDeltas: For each player visible to others, send movement/weapon/helmet/aim deltas unreliable to visible observers only
  4. ServerSkeletonSnapshot: For dead players, send respawn countdown
  5. ServerBulletSnapshot/ServerThingSnapshot: Broadcast bullets and things (unreliable or reliable based on type)
  6. ServerHeartbeat: Every ~6 ticks, send global scoreboard, ping, active player list
  7. ProcessLoop: Receive client messages (ProcessEvents → HandleMessages dispatch by MsgID)

CLIENT TICK LOOP (ClientGame.pas):
  1. Input: Capture keyboard/mouse, encode to Keys16
  2. ClientSpriteSnapshotMov: If local player moved significantly or keys changed, send unreliable snapshot with position/velocity/keys
  3. ClientSpriteSnapshot: If weapon/ammo changed, send unreliable
  4. ClientSpriteSnapshotDead: If dead, send camera focus unreliable
  5. ClientSendBullet: If client fired, send unreliable with seed
  6. ProcessLoop: Receive server messages, apply snapshots locally
  7. Render: Interpolate sprite positions using server snapshots + lag compensation, draw bullets with client-side spread

HANDSHAKE:
Client (Unit1.pas): ClientRequestGame (MsgID_RequestGame, version, anti-cheat flag) -->
Server (ServerHandleRequestGame): Validate version/password/ban/Fae capability, send error or continue
  --> ServerSyncCvars (MsgID_SyncCvars, weapon balance, cv values)
  --> ServerSendPlayList (MsgID_PlayersList, current players, map, mod)
Client: Parse PlayersList, download map/mod if needed
Client: ClientSendPlayerInfo (MsgID_PlayerInfo, colors, look, team)
Server (ServerHandlePlayerInfo): Create sprite, initialize player state
  --> ServerSendNewPlayerInfo (MsgID_NewPlayer, sprite confirmed)
Client: Parse NewPlayer, set MySprite, show team menu or auto-join
  --> Game ready, snapshots flowing

ANTI-CHEAT (Fae):
If ac_enable.Value:
  After RequestGame validation, ServerSendFaeChallenge (MsgID_FaeData, InOrder=1 for sync)
    Player.FaeSecret initialized, FaeInitChallenge generates challenge
  Client: ClientHandleFaeChallenge, calls FaeAuthSync (synchronous blocking), derives NetEncKey
  Client: ClientSendFaeResponse (MsgID_FaeData, signed response box)
  Server: ServerHandleeFaeResponse, calls FaeCheck against stored secret, validates signature/timestamp
    If valid, set Player.EncActive=True, Player.FaeResponsePending=False
    If invalid, call KickForFaeViolation, send ANTICHEAT_REJECTED via ServerSendUnAccepted
  Subsequent packets encrypted with NetEncKey (implemented in GNS layer, transparent to app)

VISIBILITY CULLING:
ServerSpriteDeltas uses PointVisible(sprite pos, observer camera pos) to only send movement to players who can see the sprite. Spectators with Port=0 (free cam) always receive all updates. Reduces bandwidth for large servers.

INTERNAL DEPS: Game.pas (Sprite array, Thing array, Bullet array, map state, team scores, vote system); Sprites.pas (TSprite class, movement, weapon application, respawn, skeleton for ragdoll); Bullets.pas (TBullet class, CreateBullet, bullet physics simulation); Things.pas (TThing class, weapon/flag pickups, ownership, timeout); Server.pas (server main loop, player database, voting, command parsing); Client.pas (local player state, demo recorder, rendering integration); Constants.pas (team IDs, game mode IDs, message type constants); Weapons.pas (weapon definitions, damage, ammo, fire rates, bullet spread); Demo.pas (demo recording/playback of network messages); FaeBase.pas / FaeRemoteAttestation.pas / FaeClient.pas / FaeRemoteAttestation.pas (anti-cheat library)

EXTERNAL DEPS: GameNetworkingSockets (Valve): UDP-based transport with reliability and ordering guarantees, connection management, statistics, Steam API: Optional integration for SteamIDs, Steam authentication, friend lists, voice data (VAC anti-cheat awareness), Protobuf-like binary encoding: Hand-coded packed records for efficient serialization (no actual protoc dependency, manual alignment)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Binary message encoding is manual hand-coded packed records with implicit size/alignment assumptions; no version tolerance if struct layout changes; protobuf would add schema versioning safety
  - Magic constants throughout (POSDELTA=20, VELDELTA=100, FIREINTERVAL_NET, MOUSEAIMDELTA) hardcoded for snapshot thresholds; brittle if gameplay changes
  - Fae anti-cheat integration is optional (ENABLE_FAE ifdef); fallback mode without encryption is vulnerable; tight coupling to FaeRemoteAttestation library
  - Bullet validation uses ad-hoc cheat checks (speed, distance, timing) rather than replay server-side simulation; impossible to catch sophisticated prediction exploits
  - ClientTickCount / ServerTickCounter / MainTickCounter syncronization is loose (no explicit clock sync protocol); large network jitter can cause temporal inconsistencies
  - Sprite/Bullet/Thing arrays are 1-indexed Pascal-style with fixed MAX_SPRITES=32, MAX_BULLETS=300, MAX_THINGS=256; no dynamic resizing, hard cap limits scalability
  - Heartbeat (global scoreboard) sent unreliable every ~6 ticks; if dropped, client may miss score/kill/death updates for 100ms, then jumps abruptly when next heartbeat arrives
  - Visibility culling (PointVisible) checks only work for rectangular maps with polygon collision; no proper frustum culling, wastes bandwidth on nearly-off-screen sprites
  - Delta compression uses simple 'has anything changed?' check rather than field-level deltas (e.g., only send health if it changed, not entire position if only ammo changed); packs unnecessary data
  - Message dispatch uses a single switch statement on MsgID (50+ cases) with no extensibility; adding new message types requires modifying Net.pas and all handler units
  - No congestion control or adaptive bitrate; sends snapshots at fixed rate regardless of network loss; could add rate limiting based on connection quality (ConnectionQuality byte is tracked but unused)
  - Chat/message flood checks use simple per-second counters; vulnerable to burst flooding if attacker sends 18+ messages in 1 second then waits
  - Duplicate bullet detection (BulletCheck ringbuffer) only checks within BULLETCHECKARRAYSIZE (~32 bullets); replay attacks possible with delays >32 bullets apart
  - Player.SpriteNum=0 used as 'not joined' sentinel but also overloaded with 'observing' state; confusing control flow
  - No retry mechanism for critical messages (map change, flag capture); if reliable channel loses packet, inconsistency until heartbeat or next major sync
  - Spectator free-cam mode (MsgID_ClientFreeCam) trusts client camera position without validation; client can send bogus position to trigger bandwidth waste or cache-busting

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How are server ticks synced with client ticks for replay? ClientTickCount is updated from server snapshots, but if client frame rate varies, the timeline becomes non-monotonic. Is this acceptable for demos?
  - Fae anti-cheat challenge has InOrder flag: what triggers async (InOrder=0) vs sync (InOrder=1)? Code shows first request is sync, but when would async occur?
  - How does PointVisible work exactly? It takes sprite X/Y and observer camera X/Y but no map/collision data visible. Is it a simple distance check or is collision checked elsewhere?
  - Why does ServerSpriteSnapshotMajor send less data (health/position only, no weapons/ammo/vest) than full snapshot? When is it used vs regular snapshot?
  - ClientSpriteSnapshot uses a simple 'has anything changed?' check but skips sending if all fields unchanged. What happens if ammo changes but nothing else? Will next snapshot be too large?
  - Bullet spread seed is seeded from server BulletSnap.Seed, but where does the original seed come from client-side? If seed collision occurs, do pellets diverge?
  - NetworkClientBullet loop-simulates bullets forward N ticks (pa = OwnerPingTick + MySprite.PingTicks). If pa > Bullet's remaining lifetime, does the loop exit early? Could cause time-travel desyncs.
  - Delta_Movement / Delta_Weapons / Delta_Helmet are sent to visible players only, but OldMovementMsg[j, i] is a 2D array. If observer j is not visible, does the cache get stale, causing next update to be sent even if no change?
  - Heartbeat is sent unreliable and includes per-player Ping array. If heartbeat is dropped multiple times, client may show stale ping values until next successful heartbeat. No retry?
  - TMsg_PlayersList has PredDuration field for predator bonus (seconds), but only used on client side for alpha/visuals. Does server track predator separately or rely on client applying bonus time?
  - FaeResponsePending flag prevents processing player info if response hasn't arrived. What timeout exists? If client never responds to Fae challenge, can it join as zombie indefinitely?
  - Chat message flood check increments MessagesASecNum[i] but resets only at next frame if under threshold. Could a client send 200 messages in 1 frame and bypass the check?
  - Duplicate bullet detection uses BulletSnap.Seed as key. Are seeds globally unique or per-weapon or per-player? If a second player fires same weapon with same seed, could it be falsely rejected?

nodes.title: [ai-bots] AI / bots
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The Bot AI subsystem in OpenSoldat provides autonomous bot players with perception, decision-making, navigation, and aiming logic. Bots perceive the game world through raycasting, choose enemies as targets, navigate via handcrafted waypoint networks, aim with difficulty-based accuracy variance, and interface with the same control mechanism as human players to execute actions.

CLIENT/SERVER: Bot AI runs exclusively on SERVER ({$IFDEF SERVER} guards ControlBot calls in Control.pas and SharedConfig.pas). Clients receive BotControl snapshots via network messages (MsgID_ClientSpriteSnapshot_Mov) containing serialized Control state; client-side Update() applies the same physical response. Bots never run on client; client sees bot movement as deterministic replay of server Control commands. Human players: client generates Control from keyboard/mouse; sends via snapshot; server uses it locally.

KEY TYPES: TControl = Boolean flags for movement (Left, Right, Up, Down), actions (Fire, Jetpack, ThrowNade, ChangeWeapon, ThrowWeapon, Reload, Prone, FlagThrow), and aim coordinates (MouseAimX, MouseAimY, MouseDist). Shared by bots and humans; populated by ControlBot() or keyboard input.; TBotData = Bot personality/state record. Stores FavWeapon, Accuracy (difficulty-scaled), Friend (ignored player name), GrenadeFreq, DeadKill (shoot corpses?), TargetNum (current enemy), CurrentWaypoint/NextWaypoint (navigation state), Camper (hide tendency), PissedOff (who is shooting me?), OnePlaceCount (stuck detector).; TWaypoint = Map node record. X, Y coordinates; Action (None, StopAndCamp, Wait1-20Second); Connections[1..20] array of next waypoint IDs; PathNum (team/objective routing); movement flags (Left, Right, Up, Down, Jetpack) to reach next waypoint.; TSprite = Dynamic entity. Contains Control field (shared input), Brain field (TBotData), Skeleton (position/velocity), BodyAnimation/LegsAnimation, Health, Weapons, Player (includes ControlMethod=HUMAN/BOT).; TWaypoints = Global waypoint database object (BotPath). Array[1..5000] of TWaypoint; FindClosest() method returns nearest waypoint within radius.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Perception via raycasting: Bot scans all active sprites; tests line-of-sight from head (Skeleton.Pos[12]) to target head with Map.RayCast() to determine visibility (distance D2); skips self, teammates (unless friendly fire), spectators, invisible sprites.; Target selection: Finds closest visible non-team/non-spectator enemy; prefers Rambo bow wielders in Rambo mode; maintains PissedOff state to track who last shot the bot; validates sightline each frame.; Combat behavior: Modulates firing, movement, crouching, jetpack based on distance buckets (DIST_TOO_CLOSE=35 to DIST_TOO_FAR=730) via SimpleDecision(). Extreme distances trigger cover-seeking or camping.; Aiming with difficulty variance: Predicts target position by scaling velocity vector by flight time (distance / weapon speed); subtracts Brain.Accuracy then adds Random(Brain.Accuracy) to inject variance. Harder difficulties (lower values) reduce accuracy term.; Difficulty scaling: bots_difficulty cvar (0-300, default 100) multiplies loaded Accuracy value: accuracy *= (difficulty / 100).
