At difficulty 10 (impossible), accuracy approaches zero variance; at 300 (stupid), high variance.; Waypoint navigation: When no enemy visible, bot follows path via CurrentWaypoint/NextWaypoint; randomly picks next connection from current waypoint's Connections array; applies waypoint movement flags (Left/Right/Up/Down/Jetpack) to Control.; Waypoint actions: Executes camp/wait logic at waypoints with StopAndCamp/Wait*Second actions; pauses movement for specified duration (OnePlaceCount counter); unsticks via jetpack if stuck >90 frames.; Path selection by game mode: CTF/INF/HTF bots pick team-specific paths (PathNum 1=Bravo attack/defend, 2=Alpha attack/defend); when carrying flag, inverts path to flee toward base.; Thing/objective seeking: Scans visible things (flags, weapons, medical kits, grenades, bows, bonus items) within DIST_FAR; if Interest>0, sets GoThing=True and calls GoToThing() to navigate to item position instead of combat.; Grenade throwing: Probabilistically throws grenades (frequency modulated by difficulty); checks distance, ammo, target position; aims based on Y-distance with gravity-based vertical adjustment.; Utility behaviors: Jumps jetpack when target above; ducks behind colliders (if difficulty<201); learns camper trait from config; reloads when ammo low; calls FreeControls() to reset state each frame.

DATA FLOW: Server-side tick loop (each frame): 1. ControlSprite(SpriteC) called for each sprite. 2. If SpriteC.Player.ControlMethod==BOT, ControlBot(SpriteC) is invoked (called from Control.pas line 296 inside {$IFDEF SERVER}). 3. ControlBot() clears prior frame's Control via FreeControls(). 4. Raycast loop (lines 547-605) tests visibility to all active sprites within map; updates Brain.TargetNum with closest visible enemy (distance D2). 5. If SeeClosest=true, SimpleDecision(SNum) runs (lines 71-456) to populate Control flags based on distance buckets and target dynamics. SimpleDecision modulates Control.Left/Right/Up/Down/Fire/Jetpack/ThrowNade and calculates Control.MouseAimX/Y with difficulty-scaled inaccuracy. 6. If SeeClosest=false, waypoint navigation runs (lines 652-862): FindClosest() locates next waypoint; selects random connection; applies waypoint movement flags to Control; handles StopAndCamp/Wait actions via OnePlaceCount counter; detects stuck state and triggers emergency jetpack. 7. Thing-seeking scan (lines 908-1003) checks for flags/weapons/items; if visible and interesting, overrides navigation with GoToThing(). 8. Grenade/knife throw logic (lines 371-398) probabilistically sets ThrowNade/ThrowWeapon based on frequency and distance. 9. Control struct (populated with all decisions) is passed to sprite Update() method which applies physics, animation, weapon firing, movement. 10. Network sends updated sprite state to clients.

INTERNAL DEPS: Sprites.pas: TSprite, TControl, TBotData structures; Update() method that executes control-driven physics; Waypoints.pas: TWaypoint, TWaypoints global object (BotPath); FindClosest() pathfinding; Game.pas: Global Sprite[] array; map/environment state; Bullets.pas: Bullet array for grenade avoidance logic; Weapons.pas: TGun records for weapon speed calculation and difficulty-aware ammo logic; Vector.pas: Vector math (vec2scale, vec2add, Distance, Sqrt) for aim prediction and navigation; Calc.pas: Distance() utility; PolyMap.pas: Map.RayCast() for line-of-sight visibility testing; Constants.pas: Weapon/bonus IDs, distance constants, game mode enums (CTF/INF/HTF/DM/etc); Cvar.pas: bots_difficulty server variable (multiplier for accuracy)

EXTERNAL DEPS: GameNetworkingSockets (Steam): Network I/O for control snapshots, PolyMap physics engine: Map collision and raycasting for visibility

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Difficulty scaling is multiplicative scalar rather than discrete skill profiles: Accuracy *= (bots_difficulty/100) is fragile; non-linear difficulty curves embedded in distance-based behavior thresholds (lines 255, 285, 379, 382, 416, 843, 853, 1010 hardcode difficulty<100/201 magic numbers).
  - Waypoint system is entirely manual authoring: Map designers must hand-place waypoints and connections; no automatic pathfinding generation. Tightly coupled to specific map layouts. Fragile if map geometry changes.
  - Hardcoded distance buckets (DIST_TOO_CLOSE=35, DIST_FAR=350, etc.) are global constants; bots cannot adapt to different weapon ranges or map scales dynamically.
  - Target selection via single raycasting pass per frame; no memory of recent targets or multi-enemy awareness; bot forgets target if LOS breaks, causing erratic refocus.
  - PissedOff mechanic (tracking who last shot me) is single-sprite state, fragile if attacker dies or disconnects; no grudge decay over time beyond 1/190 random reset (line 1070).
  - GoThing mechanic duplicates movement logic (GoToThing vs waypoint nav); messy state machine with Brain.GoThing flag.
  - No behavior trees or FSM; monolithic ControlBot() procedure mixes perception, decision, and action generation in one ~600-line function.
  - Stuck detection (OnePlaceCount) based on frame count thresholds (90 frames, 180 frames); fragile to frame rate changes.
  - Pascal OOP with object keyword and no inheritance; TSprite and TBotData are inline structs, not extensible classes.

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How does Brain.Camper trait affect bot behavior? Used in SimpleDecision to modulate cover-seeking and movement freeze, but no guidance on config file Camping values.
  - What is the purpose of Brain.Use field? Loaded from config 'OnStartUse' but never referenced in AI.pas; only seen in SharedConfig.pas line 164.
  - How is Brain.Friend validated? Loaded as string from config but checked via sprite name comparison; what if friend bot hasn't joined yet?
  - Why is WaypointTimeout checked twice (lines 1033-1040 and 1042-1049) with different conditions? Timeout resets waypoint and forces jetpack, then on next frame the stuck detection can clear waypoint again.
  - How does difficulty affect bot weapon selection? No weapon-switching logic visible in AI.pas; only mentions favorite weapon and reload hinting.
  - What happens if waypoint Actions are mixed (e.g., Wait5Seconds on a waypoint with None)? Line 834 checks Action==None for stuck detection, but Action values are mutually exclusive enum.
  - How do bots handle sloped terrain or dynamic obstacles? Waypoint system assumes static layout; no real-time pathfinding or obstacle avoidance beyond collider detection.
  - Is PissedOff state synchronized across network? Server-only variable; clients don't know which bot is 'pissed' at them, only see movement outcomes.

nodes.title: [client-rendering] Client rendering (OpenGL)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: OpenSoldat's client rendering system manages all on-screen graphics, from low-level GPU interaction (OpenGL) through texture atlasing, sprite batching, and animated properties to high-level game state visualization. It separates concerns into a graphics abstraction layer (Gfx.pas), frame composition/interpolation (GameRendering.pas), specialized rendering for map geometry and props (MapGraphics.pas), player character skeletons (GostekGraphics.pas), and UI overlays (InterfaceGraphics.pas).

CLIENT/SERVER: Client-only. All rendering is local; server sends position deltas. Interpolation is client-side prediction between tick updates. No authority/prediction separation needed—client extrapolates smoothly between authoritative states.

KEY TYPES: TGfxVertex = Single interleaved vertex: (x, y, u, v, rgba_color). 20 bytes, matched to shader attribute layout.; TGfxTexture = GPU texture resource wrapper: OpenGL handle, dimensions, format, optional FBO for render targets, MSAA sample count.; TGfxSpritesheet = Manages loading, bin-packing, and streaming of sprite images into a minimal set of GPU textures. Supports async background loading.; TGfxSprite = Sprite metadata: texture reference, normalized UV rect (TexCoords), pixel position (x,y), dimensions, scale, animation delay.; TBatch = Dynamic vertex/draw-command accumulator: buffers partial vertex data until End(), then uploads all at once to GPU.; TMapGraphics = Complete GPU representation of map: vertex+index buffers, per-layer polygon/edge draw commands, animated scenery state, minimap texture.; TGostekSprite = Single body part: image ID, skeleton bone indices (p1, p2 for bone endpoints), center offset (cx, cy), flex ratio, flip/team variants, color/alpha layers.; TInterpolationState = Snapshot of all game entity positions before interpolation; stores sprites, bullets, sparks, things to restore after rendering.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Maintain OpenGL context, shaders, blend state, dithering and MSAA settings; Manage texture life cycle: load via stb, create GPU textures, optional mipmap generation, cleanup; Batch and submit rendering: combine quads into single draw call per texture, minimize GPU state changes; Spritesheet generation: load PNG/BMP images, bin-pack into atlases, apply color keys and scaling; Render frame at variable interpolation: lerp game state between ticks for smooth 60+ FPS on 60 tick sim; Compose layered frame: background → map geometry (back) → sprites/bullets/particles → props (mid) → geometry (front) → props (front) → HUD; Render Gostek character as skeletal sprite layers: body parts positioned on bones, colored per team, equipped items visible; Draw UI overlays: health/ammo/jet bars, weapon select menus, chat, score, minimap with supersampling; Support custom interfaces via .sint archives with configurable element positions and graphics; Handle resolution changes: render-target upscaling/downscaling, interface scaling, pixel-perfect UI positioning; FreeType font rendering: glyph atlasing (lazy per-fontsize), kerning, shadow/color effects, Unicode support

DATA FLOW: 
INITIALIZATION:
  1. GfxInitContext() → SDL OpenGL, dglOpenGL binding, shader program (or fixed pipeline fallback), FT_Init
  2. LoadMainTextures() / LoadInterfaceTextures() → async sprite sheet loading via stb
  3. LoadFonts() → create FT font faces, setup glyph tables per fontsize
  4. Map.LoadGraphics() → parse map, bin-pack textures, build vertex buffers, render minimap

PER-FRAME (RenderFrame called with TimeElapsed, FramePercent [0,1]):
  1. InterpolateState(FramePercent) → Lerp all entity positions between prev and current state (on heap)
  2. UpdateProps(TimeElapsed) → cycle animated scenery sprites based on elapsed time
  3. GfxBegin() → reset batch accumulator
  4. Draw map background (6 vertices, 2 triangles) via ortho projection
  5. Draw map polygons (back layer) with Z-ordering via draw commands
  6. Draw smooth edge geometry if enabled (indexed quads)
  7. Draw bullets → each calls Bullet.Render() which adds batched quads
  8. Draw sprites (Gosteks) → RenderGostek() builds layered quads per body part, skeleton-driven positioning
  9. Draw particles → Spark.Render() adds spark quads
  10. Draw things (map props) → Thing.Render() + Thing.PolygonsRender()
  11. Draw map polygons (front layer)
  12. Draw animated scenery props via UpdateProps UV updates + index buffer draws
  13. GfxEnd() → upload all batched vertices, issue draw commands (sorted by texture)
  14. Draw HUD: RenderInterface() batches UI quads, text via glyph rasterization
  15. RestoreState() → restore interpolated positions from snapshot (undo lerp)
  16. Blit render target to screen with upscaling if needed
  17. GfxPresent() → SwapBuffers

TEXT RENDERING FLOW:
  1. GfxSetFont() → select font + size table (lazy-create if missing)
  2. ComputeGlyphs(text) → StrToGlyphs (FT char→glyph index), then per-glyph find or load from cache
  3. LoadGlyph() → FT_Load_Glyph, rasterize to bitmap, allocate in glyph texture atlas (via FindRegion)
  4. GfxDrawText() → iterate computed glyphs, bind glyph texture page, draw shadow (optional), draw text quads


INTERNAL DEPS: Game state (Sprite, Bullet, Spark, Thing entities with skeleton positions); Map data (PolyMap: polygon/texture geometry); Weapons system (weapon graphics state, ammo counts); Parts system (particle positions/velocities for bullet/spark trails); ClientGame (camera, current player, spectator mode); Input system (mouse cursor position for aim indicator); Console variables (r_zoom, r_texturefilter, r_mipmapping, r_smoothedges, r_scaleinterface, etc.)

EXTERNAL DEPS: dglOpenGL (OpenGL 1.2+ core, shader support for modern, fixed pipeline fallback for legacy), FreeType 2 (font loading, glyph rasterization, kerning), stb_image (image_free, RGBA/PNG/BMP load via PhysFS), stb_image_resize (texture downsampling for minimap), SDL2 (GL context, window, swap interval), PhysFS (virtual filesystem for mod assets)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Fixed-pipeline fallback path: dual-path shader/fixed-function code is Pascal, hard to refactor to pure modern GL/GLSL
  - Premultiply color hacks: fixed pipeline requires manual premul in fixed-function mode (workaround in SetupVertexAttributes)
  - Matrix math: 3x3 TGfxMat3 is manual 2D homogeneous coord, not reusable math library
  - Batching design: manual vertex buffer accumulation with realloc/copy; modern approach would be persistent mapped buffers or streaming
  - Glyph atlasing: node-list bin-pack is bespoke; fragmentation over time as glyphs expire from pool
  - Bone positioning: skeletal rendering tightly coupled to Gostek sprite indices (GostekGraphics.inc enum); refactoring to data-driven skeleton = major risk
  - Magic constants: GOS_RESTRICT_WIDTH, WEP_RESTRICT_HEIGHT hardcoded bounds, color indices as enum, layers as integer codes [0..2]
  - Tight asset coupling: texture IDs (GFX_GOSTEK_STOPA, etc.) baked into code via gfx.inc; swapping texture format = recompile
  - UI struct layout: TInterface is binary struct read from .sif file; layout assumptions fragile to padding/alignment changes
  - Z-ordering: props sorted by level [0..2] but no depth test; requires stable sort order = hidden invariant

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - Does the interpolation lerp happen on the original state or a copy? InterpolateState saves to heap but RestoreState restores—are there race conditions with async sprite loading?
  - How is the 3x3 matrix GfxMat3 actually applied? glUniformMatrix3fv in shader mode vs glLoadMatrixf in fixed—difference in z/w handling?
  - What triggers glyph eviction from the font page? PoolIndex wraps at GLYPH_POOL_SIZE=64, but no LRU—can old glyphs be discarded mid-frame?
  - Gostek team offset calculation: GFX_GOSTEK_TEAM2_STOPA - GFX_GOSTEK_STOPA implies texture IDs are sequential per team—is this guaranteed in gfx.inc?
  - Why does MapGraphics store AnimationsCmd as pointer-encoded (level shl 28 | index)? Is this endianness-safe?
  - PropList filtering: what defines IsPropActive()? Is it tied to prop.Enabled flag or map load distance?
  - Action snap: when CapScreen is 255 and we render action snap, do we render to ActionSnapTexture or the main target? Code path unclear around GrabActionSnap.

nodes.title: [client-io] Client audio, input, menus
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The OpenSoldat client manages player input via SDL2 keybindings, audio playback through OpenAL with spatial positioning, and menu/UI rendering through customizable widget interfaces. This subsystem bridges user interactions and server communication while maintaining consistent frame timing at 60 ticks/second.

CLIENT/SERVER: Client-only. All input processing, audio playback, menu rendering, and UI state management occur entirely on client. Camera position (CameraX/Y) and sound listener updates are client-side computed. Input actions (chat, team change, weapon select) are packaged into network messages and sent to server for validation. Server does not render anything—all rendering is client-side via GameRendering module using OpenGL. Chat text is transmitted as MSGTYPE_PUB/TEAM/RADIO packets. Demo playback is client-local (no network involvement).

KEY TYPES: TAction = Scoped enum: None, Left, Right, Jump, Crouch, Fire, Jet, Reload, ChangeWeapon, VoiceChat, ThrowGrenade, DropWeapon, Prone, FlagThrow, StatsMenu, GameStats, MiniMap, PlayerName, FragsList, SniperLine, Radio, RecordDemo, VolumeUp/Down, MouseSensitivity, Cmd, Chat, TeamChat, Snap, Weapons, Bind. Maps SDL keycodes to gameplay actions.; TBind = Record containing Action (TAction), keyId (LongWord or 300+mousebutton), keyMod (KM_ALT|KM_CTRL|KM_SHIFT), and Command (WideString). Links key combos to actions and custom commands.; TGameButton = Menu button record: Active (Boolean), x1/y1/x2/y2 (Integer coordinates), Caption (WideString). Defines clickable menu areas.; TGameMenu = Menu container record: Active (Boolean), x/y position, w/h dimensions, Button array. Represents a modal/overlay menu (ESC, Team, Limbo, Kick, Map).; TSoundSample = Record: Loaded (Boolean), Buffer (ALuint OpenAL buffer ID). Wraps decoded WAV data in GPU memory.; TInterface = HUD layout record: Alpha (Byte), visibility flags (Health, Ammo, Vest, Jet, Nades, etc.), component positions/rotations, bar dimensions, alignment (left/right). Defines screen layout for customizable UIs.; TFrameTiming = Timing state: Frequency, StartTime, PrevTime, PrevRenderTime, Accumulator, MinDeltaTime, Elapsed (all Extended for high precision), Counter, Fps, FpsAccum. Fixed-timestep simulation with variable-rate rendering.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Map SDL2 keyboard/mouse events to game actions via key binding lookup (FindKeyBind with modifier matching); Execute bound actions: weapon changes, chat modes, menu navigation, voice chat start, sensitivity/volume adjustment; Initialize OpenAL device/context, load 163 WAV samples (guns, explosions, footsteps, UI sounds) from PhysFS archive; Maintain 256 OpenAL sources with spatial positioning (AL_POSITION relative to listener), distance attenuation (SOUND_MAXDIST), and looping flags; Render in-game UI: health/ammo/jet/vest bars, weapon display, chat messages, player names, minimap, stats overlay with customizable layouts; Manage modal menus: ESC menu (exit/map/kick/team), Team selection, Weapon limbo, Map/Kick voting with button hover states; Execute console commands via ParseInput bridge: bind, connect, say, record, mute, and custom bindings; Maintain chat input state machine (chat type, cursor position, tab completion, clipboard paste) with 256-char limit; Control main game loop timing: 60 tick/second fixed simulation, frame accumulator for variable FPS rendering, demo playback sync; Handle window focus/focus-loss (SDL_WINDOW_INPUT_FOCUS checks), mouse relative mode for aiming, fullscreen/windowed resolution scaling; Load customizable interface archives (.sint files mounted via PhysFS), scale UI for ultrawide/4K displays (r_scaleinterface cvar)

DATA FLOW: Entry: StartGame initializes SDL2, PhysFS mounts game archives, InitSound creates OpenAL context, LoadSounds decodes all WAV samples into buffers. InitGameMenus/InitGameGraphics create widget state. StartGameLoop enters infinite loop calling (1) GameInput via ControlGame.GameInput polling SDL_PollEvent, (2) GameLoop from ClientGame updating frame timing/ticks, calling Update_Frame to refresh sprites/bullets/weather, then rendering. GameInput processes SDL_KEYDOWN/KEYUP by looking up key binding via FindKeyBind(KeyMods, ScanCode) returning PBind. If bound, executes action (weapon select, menu toggle, chat start, volume adjust). SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN/UP set KeyStatus[button+300]. SDL_MOUSEMOTION applies cl_sensitivity delta to mx/my camera target. SDL_TEXTINPUT appends to ChatText if chat active. Update_Frame runs sprite/bullet physics, plays spatial audio via FPlaySound(SampleNum, ListenerX/Y, EmitterX/Y, Channel), updates menu hover states. Rendering calls RenderInterface to composite HUD bars, text, and menu overlays. Exit via GameMenuAction callback (menu button press) or SDL_QUITEV event.

INTERNAL DEPS: SDL2 (video init, window, event polling, relative mouse mode, clipboard, message boxes); OpenAL (device/context creation, buffer/source management, 3D positioning); PhysFS (archive mounting, file reading for sounds, configs, interfaces); GameRendering (sprite rendering, texture management, frame buffer); Sprites/Game/Weapons (sprite state, weapon definitions, constants); NetworkClientConnection/Messages (server communication for chat, team change, voting); Demo (demo record/playback integration); Console (message display, command history); Command/Cvar (configuration and console variable management)

EXTERNAL DEPS: SDL2 (input events, window management, audio specs, file I/O via SDL_RWops), OpenAL (spatial audio, buffer/source objects, looping, gain/attenuation), PhysFS (virtual filesystem, archive mounting), FreeType (font rendering for UI text, presumed via GameRendering), GameNetworkingSockets or custom UDP (network I/O for server communication)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Input.pas uses global KeyStatus array[512] and dynamic Binds array with linear search in FindKeyBind—should be hash map for 1000+ keybindings
  - Sound.pas hardcodes 163 samples by index (SFX_AK74_FIRE=1, etc.) in SAMPLE_FILES array; refactoring to string names would require careful enum migration
  - GameMenus uses absolute screen coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2) for buttons—scaling to different resolutions requires manual offset recalculation per menu
  - TBind.Command is WideString executed via ParseInput with no syntax validation—injection risk if bindings allow arbitrary command chains
  - OpenAL source management uses simple linear search in FPlaySound to find free sources—should use queue/pool for predictable performance
  - Chat input mixes SDL_TextInput and SDL_KEYDOWN handlers with overlapping state (ChatText, CursorPosition, CompletionBase)—prone to edge cases
  - Frame timing uses integer Accumulator ticks without double-precision—floating-point drift could cause desync in long sessions
  - Menu visibility globals (EscMenu, TeamMenu, LimboMenu) are singletons with implicit state—refactor to state machine enum
  - UI scaling via _RScala/_IScala cvars applied ad-hoc throughout InterfaceGraphics—no abstraction layer for resolution-independent rendering
  - Hard dependency on 60 ticks/second (GOALTICKS=60) baked into Game.pas constants—would require cascading rewrites to support variable tick rates

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How does relative mouse mode (SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode) interact with menu mouse clicks—is there a toggle in GameMenuClick()?
  - Voice chat buffer queue (VoiceBufferQueue in STEAM ifdef) uses TFPGList<LongWord>—is this thread-safe relative to mic data capture?
  - FPlaySound distant sound effect logic (lines 425-441) references GrenadeEffectTimer for attenuation—is this server-synchronized or client-computed?
  - Weapon limbo menu (LimboMenu) uses InitButton relative positioning—what happens to button hit areas if font size changes?
  - Why does BindKey set length twice (line 59, 91)—is the empty slot at length-1 intentional or a bug?
  - How is ActionSnapTaken synchronized with ScreenCounter=255 in the snap action handler?
  - Chat autocomplete (TabComplete) searches all MAX_PLAYERS sprites every tab press—is there a frame-budget concern?
  - PhysFS_readBuffer for WAV files (LoadSample line 124) allocates memory—is it freed after SDL_LoadWAV_RW or leaked?
  - Demo playback updates sprites but KeyStatus remains SDL-driven—are demo replays affected by current input state?
  - How does r_scaleinterface affect mouse click coordinates in GameMenuClick—is there coordinate transformation?

nodes.title: [server-infra] Server infrastructure
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The OpenSoldat dedicated server is a standalone network multiplayer game server written in FreePascal that manages game state, player connections, map rotation, anti-cheat enforcement, ban management, and administrative remote control. It hosts gameplay for up to 32 players across multiple game modes (Deathmatch, CTF, Team Match, etc.) and communicates with master-server/lobby registration systems and optional file servers for client downloads.

CLIENT/SERVER: Server-authoritative architecture. Client sends input (movement, weapon fire, team change); server validates and executes, then broadcasts outcomes. Sprites are global mutable state on server; client receives periodic snapshots (position, velocity, health, animation frame). Bans/password/admin lists live on server only. RCON is server-facing TCP only (no client connection). Lobby registration is server-initiated HTTP. FileServer is optional server component. Deterministic voting (kick/map) happens on server with client vote tallying. Player stats and logs are server-side-only.

KEY TYPES: TServerNetwork = Inherits TNetwork; manages UDP/GNS listen socket, peer connections, message polling, and per-player network stats; CreateTServerNetwork(host, port) binds to address; TAdminServer = TThread-based TCP server for RCON; owns FAdmins (TThreadList of TAdminServerConnectionThread), FMessageQueue for command serialization, bucket-rate limiter (FBucketTokens/FBucketRate/FBucketBurst); TAdminServerConnectionThread = Per-admin connection; authenticates with password, reads line-buffered commands from TSocketStream, enqueues TAdminMessage records to shared queue, calls ParseInput(255) for privileged commands; TMsg_RefreshX = RCON data structure echoed by ProcessCommands; packed array-of-array structure carrying player names/stats, flag positions, team scores, map info for admin monitoring; TBanIP / TBanHW = Packed records in dynamic arrays BannedIPList/BannedHWList; each stores IP (supports wildcards via fpmasks.MatchesMask), Time (PERMANENT or secondes remaining), Reason string; TPlayer = Per-connection player object; attached to GNS peer's m_nConnUserData; owns Name, Team, IP, Port, SteamID, HardwareID, statistics (Kills/Deaths/Ping), control method (HUMAN/BOT), mute/TK warning flags; TLobbyThread = TThread-based HTTP client; creates JSON payload from game state and POSTs to sv_lobbyurl/v0/servers/register; spawns once per minute in ServerLoop; TFileServer / THTTPServerThread = TFPHTTPServer instance in dedicated thread; validates Content-Type and User-Agent, serves file streams with attachment headers from /maps and /mods paths, supports Steam Workshop item download; TMsg_RequestGame / TMsg_PlayerInfo = Handshake packets; RequestGame carries version, password, HW ID, anti-cheat type; PlayerInfo carries name, colors, team, appearance flags; TSprite = In-game player avatar; owns skeleton/pos/velocity, active weapon, health, team, stats; networked to clients via periodic ServerSpriteSnapshot messages; bound to TPlayer via Sprite[i].Player

RESPONSIBILITIES: Accept and validate incoming client connection requests (IP, password, version, ban status, anti-cheat); Allocate and initialize player sprites and TPlayer instances upon successful handshake; Manage game tick loop (AppOnIdle -> UpdateFrame) at tunable rates (LAN 60Hz vs. Internet variable 30-100ms snapshots); Broadcast networked game state: sprite snapshots (position/velocity/animation), bullet trajectories, thing (item) positions, flag state, scores; Process client input (movement, shooting, chat, team changes) and maintain authoritative game physics; Enforce server rules: flood detection (messages/sec), ping limits, chat limits, anti-cheat challenges (FAE); Detect and handle player disconnections (no response timeout, kick for non-responsiveness to anti-cheat); Manage bot spawning/AI and auto-balancing teams on player joins/leaves; Execute map rotation and forced map changes after time/score limits; Implement IP and Hardware ID ban system with time-based expiry, file persistence, wildcard matching; Provide TCP-based RCON interface with password authentication and bucket-rate limiting; Execute admin/console commands (kick, ban, nextmap, say, etc.) with privilege checks; Register server with master-server lobby on configurable interval (JSON HTTP POST); Optionally host HTTP file server for map/mod downloads with client version validation; Log game events (kills, flag caps, joins, disconnects) to rotating text files; Maintain server config (cvars) and save/load from .ini files; sync gamemode-relevant cvars to all clients; Support optional scripting engine (PascalScript) callbacks for custom game logic; Optional Steam integration: authentication, stats, Workshop map downloads, voice chat

DATA FLOW: Server startup: Main.RunServer -> ActivateServer (load config/maps/bans) -> StartServer (bind network, spawn bots, spawn lobby thread) -> Main loop: while ProgReady AppOnIdle(). Per-frame: (1) UDP.ProcessLoop receives packets into TServerNetwork, dispatches ServerHandleRequestGame/PlayerInfo/movement messages; (2) AdminServer.ProcessCommands drains RCON message queue serially; (3) UpdateFrame updates all sprites/bullets/things physics, checks map-change/ban-expiry timers; (4) Network snapshot broadcasts: every 30-100ms send ServerSpriteSnapshot (position/velocity/animation) to all peers, major snapshots every 60-200ms. Per-message: HandleMessages unpacks bitstream, routes to ServerHandleXxx procedures which modify game state (Sprite[], Thing[], TeamScore) and may enqueue outbound ServerSendXxx calls. RCON flow: TAdminServerConnectionThread.Execute reads lines, queues TAdminMessage, ProcessCommands calls ParseInput(255) which dispatches CommandXxx callbacks. Flood/ban/lobby updates: MainTickCounter-modulo triggers UpdateIPBanList (every 60s), LobbyThread.Create (every 60s), ping warnings (every 6s), chat flood warnings (every 1s).

INTERNAL DEPS: shared/network/Net.pas (TServerNetwork base); shared/network/NetworkServerConnection.pas (handshake, handoff to sprites); shared/network/NetworkServerGame.pas (game message handlers); shared/network/NetworkServerMessages.pas (message type definitions); shared/network/NetworkServerSprite.pas (player snapshot transmission); shared/network/NetworkServerThing.pas (items/flags transmission); shared/Game.pas (TSprite, TThing, TBullet physics); shared/Weapons.pas (weapon definitions, ammo); Cvar.pas, Command.pas (cvar system and command dispatcher); BanSystem.pas (IP/HW ban lists); LogFile.pas (logging infrastructure); Demo.pas (demo recording); ServerHelper.pas (utility functions); Constants.pas (magic numbers, message IDs, game modes); Steam.pas (optional Steam API bindings); ScriptDispatcher.pas (optional PascalScript callbacks)

EXTERNAL DEPS: GameNetworkingSockets (GNS): peer-to-peer UDP-based reliable messaging with connection management via SteamAPI handles, Steam API (optional, conditional IFDEF STEAM): authentication, stats, Workshop UGC, FPHTTPServer (fphttpserver unit): HTTP server implementation for FileServer, Sockets / Ssockets (FreePascal RTL): TCP socket layer for RCON, PhysFS (PhysFS.pas): virtual file system for .smod/.smap archive mounting, FreePascal RTL: SysUtils, Classes, Threads (TThread), file I/O

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Pascal global state: ServerLoop.pas uses many globals (MainTickCounter, Sprite[], Bullet[], Thing[], TeamScore, MuteList) that would require refactoring into a game-state struct for multithreading safety or modularity
  - Magic tick counts: Hard-coded intervals (MainTickCounter mod 1000, mod SECOND*6, etc.) scattered in ServerLoop; no centralized event/timer abstraction
  - RCON blocking socket design: TAdminServerConnectionThread uses blocking socket reads in a loop; migration to async/non-blocking would require rewrite
  - Tight coupling: ServerCommands callback functions directly call KickPlayer, NextMap, etc. modifying global state; no abstraction layer for testing
  - Ban list efficiency: BannedIPList/BannedHWList are linear-scanned arrays with no indexing; O(n) lookup on join could bottleneck large ban lists
  - String-based command parsing: ParseInput uses AnsiString splitting and case-insensitive command names; no type-safe command registry
  - File I/O blocking: SaveBannedList, SaveTxtLists use blocking TextFile writes in main loop; should be async or background thread
  - Deprecated message types: Old message IDs (MsgID_ClientSpriteSnapshot_Mov, MsgID_Delta_*) suggest protocol versioning; unclear removal schedule
  - Hardcoded LAN/Internet rates: net_lan cvar switches entire behavior; should be more flexible per-connection config
  - Steam coupling: $IFDEF STEAM wraps large code paths; no clean abstraction for non-Steam auth systems
  - Pascal-ism: Record-based message structures (TMsg_RefreshX) with fixed-size arrays and packed layout are fragile and hard to extend

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - What is the exact format of the legacy .bot config files loaded by RandomBot and AddBotPlayer? Are bots NavMesh-based or deterministic script-based?
  - How does the script engine (ScriptDispatcher) integrate with the network loop? Are callbacks synchronous or async? Can scripts block the main loop?
  - What is the anti-cheat FAE subsystem? Is it server-side state validation, client-side challenge-response, or both? How does KICK_AC vs. KICK_CHEAT differentiate?
  - How is game determinism guaranteed across demos and replays? Does demo recording use recorded client input or server snapshots?
  - What is the purpose of OldHelmetMsg array and the Delta_Helmet message type? Is it for optimized state synchronization?
  - Are voice chat messages (MsgID_VoiceData) transmitted peer-to-peer via GNS or proxied through the server?
  - How does the Steam Workshop integration work for custom maps? Are downloaded maps persisted locally or streamed?
  - What is the exact CSV format of logs/kills/*.txt? How are kill stats aggregated for long-running servers?
  - Why are RemoteAdmins and AdminIPs separate lists? What is the distinction between remote admin (RCON) and game admin (request password)?
  - How does DemoRecorder.SaveNextFrame work? Is it recording full game state or just client inputs?

nodes.title: [scripting] Scripting / modding (PascalScript)
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: ScriptCore is OpenSoldat's server-side scripting subsystem that allows server administrators to extend game functionality via Pascal scripts. It consists of two versions (legacy ScriptCore and modern ScriptCore3) that compile and execute Pascal code in a sandboxed environment using PascalScript, providing event-driven APIs for manipulating game state, players, maps, bullets, and other entities while enforcing security restrictions based on sandbox levels.

CLIENT/SERVER: Server-side only. Scripts run on dedicated server, access game state directly, no network transmission of script code or execution results (except indirect effects on game state visible to all clients). Event dispatch is synchronous and blocking on main server thread.

KEY TYPES: TScript = Abstract base class defining the event interface (OnPlayerDamage, OnJoinTeam, OnPlayerKill, OnVoteMapStart, etc.) and basic script lifecycle (Prepare, Launch, CallFunc); TScriptDispatcher = Singleton managing all script instances; discovers scripts via check functions, coordinates event dispatch, maintains script registry with locking, queues script unregistration; TScriptCore = Legacy ScriptCore (v1) extending TPascalCore; compiles source via Includes.txt mechanism, uses TPSScript directly, implements all event handlers; TScriptCore3 = Modern ScriptCore (v2) extending TScript; config.ini driven, uses TPascalCompiler/TPascalExec for bytecode, supports sandbox levels (0=full, 1=no DLLs, 2+=restricted); TPascalCompiler = Wrapper around uPSCompiler; compiles Pascal source to bytecode, manages search paths/defines, coordinates API registration at compile-time; TPascalExec = Wrapper around uPSRuntime.TPSExec; executes bytecode, loads/registers APIs at runtime, manages initialization/finalization sections; TScriptActivePlayer = Player wrapper exposing sprite data (Health, Vest, Weapons, Colors, Admin, Dummy status) with event callbacks for damage/kill/respawn; TScriptGame = Game state wrapper (GameStyle, MaxPlayers, Maps, Gravity, ScoreLimit, TimeLimit, Teams) with control methods (Shutdown, StartVote, LoadWeap, LoadCon, LoadList, StartRecord); TScriptMap = Map wrapper providing access to Objects, Bullets, SpawnPoints, Flags via arrays/methods; includes RayCast and CreateBullet physics methods; TScriptCore3Conf = Configuration object holding SandboxLevel, AllowDlls, AllowIniEdit flags, SearchPaths, and Defines read from config.ini; TScriptFileAPI = File I/O API enforcing sandbox-based path restrictions; wraps TStringList, TMemIniFile, TMemoryStream with CheckAccess validation; ICompilerAPI / IRuntimeAPI = Interfaces allowing modular API registration; each API module (ScriptGame, ScriptMap, ScriptFileAPI, etc.) implements these to register functions/variables

RESPONSIBILITIES: Discover and load scripts from 'scripts/' subdirectory; validate script structure (Includes.txt for v1, config.ini for v3); Compile Pascal source code to bytecode using PascalScript compiler with optional DLL support; Register sandboxed API surface to scripts (Game, Map, Players, Weapons, Bullets, File I/O, Math utilities); Execute scripts in response to server events (OnPlayerDamage, OnJoinTeam, OnPlayerKill, OnMapChange, OnVoteMapStart, etc.); Dispatch events to all registered scripts sequentially with proper locking to prevent race conditions; Enforce sandbox security: restrict file I/O based on sandbox level, prevent DLL access unless enabled, validate INI edits; Handle script errors: log exceptions, optionally disable script, recompile on crash, or shutdown server based on sc_onscriptcrash cvar; Provide cross-script communication via CallFunc (e.g., 'OtherScript.SomeFunction'); Manage script lifecycle: prepare (compile), launch (activate), tick (periodic callbacks), shutdown (finalization); Support both legacy ScriptCore (v1 with direct TPSScript) and modern ScriptCore3 (v2 with bytecode) in dispatcher

DATA FLOW: Main event flow: Server event occurs (e.g., player takes damage) -> ScriptDispatcher.OnPlayerDamage() called -> iterates FScripts list -> calls TScript.OnPlayerDamage() on each -> locks/unlocks via DoLock()/DoUnlock() based on thread ID -> each script executes event handler via CallFunc() -> script function may modify damage value or perform side effects -> returns to dispatcher -> dispatcher accumulates return value. Per-script flow: Prepare() reads source/config, calls TPascalCompiler.Compile() which preprocesses includes/defines, registers API functions via OnUses/ICompilerAPI, produces bytecode. Launch() calls TPascalExec.LoadBytecode() which registers API functions via IRuntimeAPI, calls initialization sections. OnClockTick events called at MainTickCounter intervals configured per-script. Synchronization: Each TScript has FLock (TCriticalSection), DoLock/DoUnlock acquired on non-main-thread event dispatch.

INTERNAL DEPS: ScriptDispatcher (central event coordinator); PascalCore (base for v1 scripts); PascalCompiler (bytecode generation); PascalExec (bytecode execution); PascalDebugger (error reporting with source info); Script API modules: ScriptGame, ScriptMap, ScriptPlayer, ScriptWeapon, ScriptBullet, ScriptTeam, ScriptMapsList, ScriptBanLists, ScriptSpawnPoint, ScriptObject, ScriptUnit, ScriptGlobal, ScriptCoreFunctions, ScriptFileAPI, ScriptMath, ScriptDateUtils; ScriptCore3Api (base API interface); ScriptExceptions (exception handling); ScriptCoreInterface (legacy API functions for v1); Server, Game, Sprites, Things, Bullets, Weapons modules (game state access)

EXTERNAL DEPS: PascalScript (uPSRuntime, uPSCompiler, uPSComponent, uPSDebugger, uPSUtils, uPSC_std, uPSC_dll, uPSR_std, uPSR_dll, uPSPreProcessor from 3rdparty/pascalscript/Source/), FPC runtime (Classes, SysUtils, syncobjs for threading), RegExpr (regex support in scripts), IniFiles (config.ini parsing)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Heavy Pascal-ism: pointer syntax (@), untyped variant arrays, property setters with side effects, global state (MainTickCounter, Sprite[], Bullet[] arrays accessed directly)
  - Tight coupling: API modules directly access global game state (Sprite, Bullet, Map, Game, Server globals); no dependency injection; Server/Game modules imported by every API wrapper
  - Global synchronization: Single dispatcher lock protects all scripts; no per-script or per-event granularity; FLock acquired at event boundary not within event handler
  - Magic constants: MAX_THINGS, MAX_BULLETS, MAX_SPAWNPOINTS, MAX_PLAYERS hard-coded in multiple files; weapon enum conversions (weap2obj, obj2weap, etc.) with hardcoded switch statements
  - Undocumented invariants: Event dispatch order matters (scripts executed in registration order, damage modifiers cascade); cross-script CallFunc format 'ScriptName.FunctionName' not enforced at type-level; sandbox level logic scattered across multiple files
  - Two versions maintained in parallel: ScriptCore (v1) and ScriptCore3 (v2) both active, separate code paths, different compilation/execution models, complicates future changes
  - PascalScript quirks: 32-bit bytecode format, limited type system, variant-based FFI, custom exception handling in OnException callback, compiler preprocessor integration
  - File sandbox bypassing: Path validation in ScriptFileAPI.CheckAccess() based on string prefix matching; relative path traversal possible if not carefully checked (AnsiReplaceStr checking for '..' is insufficient)
  - Error resilience: Crashed script can trigger server shutdown or recompile loop; no isolation; script error in OnClockTick could block all subsequent event processing

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How exactly does the two-version dispatch work? Does ScriptDispatcher maintain both v1 and v3 scripts simultaneously and call both on events? Or is it switched at compile time?
  - What is the exact sandbox level model? ScriptCore3.pas reads it as integer 0-2+, but only found documented mentions of 'Sandboxed' config in CheckFunction. What do levels 0, 1, 2, 3... actually restrict?
  - Why does ScriptCore.OnPlayerDamage convert to Integer(Round(Damage)) while passing Single damage elsewhere? Does this truncate precision or is there a reason?
  - How does hybrid/legacy mode in ScriptCore3 work? SetHybridMode() is called but implementation not visible in read portion.
  - What are the initialization/finalization sections triggered in TPascalExec? Are these !MAIN_ and !FINISH_ sections automatically called per script, or per unit?
  - Is there any mechanism to limit script CPU time, memory usage, or prevent infinite loops? Or do runaway scripts just block the main server thread?
  - How are script API class instances (TScriptGame, TScriptMap, etc.) lifecycle-managed? Are they created once at startup and reused, or created per script?
  - The CheckFunction(Dir) pattern returns TScript or nil. How are multiple version's CheckFunctions tried? Does first-match win?
  - What does sc_onscriptcrash cvar control exactly? Values are 'shutdown', 'recompile', 'disable'. Is there a 'continue' mode?
  - In ScriptFileAPI, path validation checks SandboxLevel. How are search paths resolved? Can scripts escape via symlinks?

nodes.title: [config-console] Console / Cvar / Command config
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: The console, cvar, and command system in OpenSoldat provides a unified configuration interface for engine/gameplay settings with multi-layered support for client-server synchronization, persistence, and validation. Cvars (console variables) are the core abstraction for configurable parameters; commands implement console actions; the console displays output; and logging captures events to disk. The system bridges scripting, networking, and in-game UI.

CLIENT/SERVER: Client: declares cl_*, ui_*, r_*, demo_*, snd_* cvars; loads client.cfg; client-side callbacks (r_zoomChange, demo_speedChange, snd_volumeChange, cl_player_wepChange); receives CVAR_SYNC cvars from server; MainConsole/BigConsole display; logs to consolelog-*.txt. Server: declares sv_*, net_*, bots_*, sc_*, fileserver_* cvars; loads server.cfg; server-side callbacks (sv_gravityChange, killlimitChange); broadcasts CVAR_SYNC cvars to all clients on changes (via CvarsNeedSyncing + network sync); outputs to stdout + RCON; logs to consolelog-*.txt. Shared: Cvars unit defines types; Command unit ParseInput() works on both; Console/LogFile conditional compilation (#IFDEF SERVER) routes output differently. Authority: server owns CVAR_SERVER settings (clients cannot set); clients can query but not modify server cvars in ParseInput on client side (line 408-411 Command.pas 'ignore server-related cvars on client').

KEY TYPES: TCvarBase = Abstract base class for all cvars; provides Name, Flags (set of TCvarFlag), Description, GetErrorMessage(); ParseAndSetValue() parses string input; ValueAsString() for display; Reset() reverts to default; TCvar<T> = Generic cvar class with FValue (current) and FDefaultValue; TCallback for change hooks; SetValue() invokes callback, validates, marks CVAR_MODIFIED if changed; TIntegerCvar = Cvar<Integer> with FMinValue/FMaxValue bounds checking; SetValue() enforces range; on server, raises SyncUpdate(True) if value changed; TSingleCvar = Cvar<Single> with float bounds checking and FormatFloat display; TBooleanCvar = Cvar<Boolean> parsing from '1'/'0' strings; TColorCvar = Cvar<TColor> for RGB color values stored as hex ($RRGGBB); TStringCvar = Cvar<AnsiString> with FMinLength/FMaxLength constraints; TCommand = Record with Name, FunctionPtr (procedure), Description, Flags (set of TCommandFlag); stored in Commands hashlist; TConsole = Object type (not class) with TextMessage/TextMessageColor arrays (CONSOLE_MAX_MESSAGES), Count, scroll state; ConsoleAdd(), Console() overloads; GetContentsAsPlainText(); TCvarFlag = enum: CVAR_IMMUTABLE (read-only after set), CVAR_ARCHIVE (write to cfg), CVAR_SPONLY (singleplayer only), CVAR_NOTIFY (notify players on change), CVAR_MODIFIED (flag set when changed), CVAR_CLIENT (client-owned), CVAR_SERVER (server-owned), CVAR_SYNC (sync to clients), CVAR_SCRIPT (set by script), CVAR_INITONLY (only at startup), CVAR_TOSYNC (temporary flag for pending sync); TCommandFlag = enum: CMD_INIT, CMD_ALIAS, CMD_SCRIPT, CMD_DEFERRED (defer until DeferredInitialized=true), CMD_ADMINONLY, CMD_PLAYERONLY

RESPONSIBILITIES: Cvar registry: define/register cvars by type (Integer, Single, Boolean, Color, String) with bounds and default values; Config file loading: parse text .cfg files (server.cfg, client.cfg) with comment support via exec command; Command dispatch: unify command execution and cvar value changes under ParseInput() interface; Value validation: enforce min/max bounds, length constraints, type conversions; callbacks for side effects; Network synchronization: track CVAR_SYNC cvars marked as changed (CVAR_TOSYNC), serialize to binary, broadcast to clients; Persistence flags: mark cvars for archival (CVAR_ARCHIVE) or server-only (CVAR_SERVER) or initialization-only (CVAR_INITONLY); Console message queuing: buffer text messages with colors, timestamps, fading/scrolling effects; Logging to disk: background writer for game events with thread-safe buffering and throttling; Command aliases: support user-defined command shortcuts mapping to multi-command sequences; Authorization: enforce admin-only (CMD_ADMINONLY, CVAR_SERVER) and player-only restrictions on command/cvar access; Deferred execution: defer commands until initialization complete for boot-up safety; Internationalization: wrap strings through translation system (GameStrings._)

DATA FLOW: Startup: CvarInit() called → creates Cvars/CvarsSync TFPHashLists → calls .Add() for each cvar (registers in Cvars, adds CVAR_SYNC types to CvarsSync) → CommandInit() registers built-in commands (echo, exec, cmdlist, cvarlist, reset, alias, toggle, inc). Config loading: LoadConfig('server.cfg' or 'client.cfg') opens file → reads line-by-line → skips '//' comments → calls ParseInput(line) for each. ParseInput: tokenizes input by ' ' delimiter → if token[0] matches command name, execute via CommandPtr^.FunctionPtr() → else lookup as cvar via TCvarBase.Find() → if cvar: get (display value) or set (ParseAndSetValue + error reporting). Cvar change: SetValue() validates → calls OnChange callback (if assigned) → on success: updates FValue, marks CVAR_MODIFIED if != default → on server: if value changed, calls SyncUpdate(True) to set CVAR_TOSYNC flag and CvarsNeedSyncing=true. Network sync: server main loop checks CvarsNeedSyncing → iterates CvarsSync list → for each cvar with CVAR_TOSYNC: serializes to binary stream (8-bit index + typed value) → sends TMsg_ServerSyncCvars packet to connected players → clears CVAR_TOSYNC flag. Logging: Console output (MainConsole.Console() on client, MainConsole.Console() on server) → calls AddLineToLogFile(GameLog, msg) → if log_enable: buffers to TStringList → if log_level>1: calls WriteLogFile() to flush to disk. Debug/trace: Debug() and Trace() procs call WriteLn() if log_level >= LEVEL_DEBUG or LEVEL_TRACE. Console display (client): ConsoleAdd() increments Count, stores TextMessage[Count]/TextMessageColor[Count], sets ScrollTick=-NewMessageWait → rendering loop scrolls message history via ScrollConsole(). Admin/authorization: on server, CMD_ADMINONLY/CVAR_SERVER commands checked against IsAdminIP(Sender.IP) before execution.

INTERNAL DEPS: Constants (MAX_CVARS, CONSOLE_MAX_MESSAGES, color codes, message types); Util (directory/path utilities, color parsing); Classes/Contnrs (TFPHashList, TStringList); SysUtils (string conversion, file I/O); Game (sprite/player state for callbacks like sv_gravityChange); Sound (for snd_volumeChange callback); Net/UDP (for TMsg_ServerSyncCvars network packet sending); LogFile/TraceLog (for output); IniFiles (for SharedConfig.pas bot/weapon loading)

EXTERNAL DEPS: SDL2 (if renderer settings like r_fullscreen affect video backend), OpenGL (r_compatibility, r_texturefilter, r_msaa cvars affect rendering), Steam (sv_setsteamaccount, cl_voicechat, fs_workshop_* cvars; SteamWarning callback), PhysFS (PHYSFS_readAsStream used in GameStrings for localization .mo files), FreeType (font cvars like font_1_name, font_1_filename interact with font loader)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - TFPHashList is case-sensitive hash table; cvar names lowercased at Add() but some inconsistency (TSingleCvar.Add line 437 uses Name not CvarName for sync list)
  - Callback signatures vary (function pointers as 'var Cvar: TCvarBase' vs just 'Cvar:' inconsistently)
  - No built-in config write/save: CVAR_ARCHIVE flag marked but no implementation found for writing modified cvars back to .cfg files
  - Global cvar variable declarations scattered across Server.pas and Client.pas (not in Cvar.pas) making refactoring risky
  - CvarsInitialized and CvarsNeedSyncing are global booleans (no thread synchronization in LogFile/Console uses)
  - Deferred command execution (CMD_DEFERRED) tied to CvarsInitialized global flag; unclear initialization order dependency
  - Console output not thread-safe on server ('NOTE: not thread save!' comment in Console.pas line 107); LogLock only protects LogFile, not console itself
  - ParseInput tokenization naive (splits on space, no quote handling); aliases work around with semicolon delimiter but fragile
  - OnChange callbacks can return false to reject change but error message handling inconsistent (GetErrorMessage clears after read)
  - Color cvar parsing uses StrToIntDef default to $000000; no validation that string is hex (line 616 Cvar.pas)
  - Timestamp in log files hardcoded 'yy/mm/dd hh:nn:ss' format (no configurability)
  - No cvar deprecation/versioning mechanism; old config keys silently ignored

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - Where are modified cvars (CVAR_ARCHIVE) written back to config files? No SaveConfig() or WriteConfig() found; only LoadConfig() exists.
  - What is the difference between Cvars and CvarsSync TFPHashLists? CvarsSync contains subset with CVAR_SYNC flag; but why are all cvars in Cvars yet only some in CvarsSync?
  - Why does Console.pas have separate code paths for SERVER (WriteLn to stdout + RCON broadcast) and CLIENT (MainConsole/BigConsole) but also shared MainConsole.Console calls? How does MainConsole differ on each side?
  - When is CvarsInitialized set to true? Assumed during CvarInit() or after config loading, but code checks not found.
  - How do commands with CMD_DEFERRED flag interact with server startup? ParseInput defers them to DeferredCommands, then RunDeferredCommands() at some point—where called?
  - What triggers the network sync of CvarsSync? Server sets CVAR_TOSYNC flag in SetValue(), then main loop must check CvarsNeedSyncing—where is that check in the tick/update loop?
  - How are client-received CVAR_SYNC values unpacked? NetworkClientConnection.pas not examined; assume reads stream and calls SetValue() on each.
  - Do aliased commands (CMD_ALIAS) support nested aliases or circular references? CommandExecuteAlias splits on ';' but no recursion guard visible.
  - What is the intended behavior when a CVAR_IMMUTABLE cvar is modified? SetValue() checks flag but where is it used? No cvars marked CVAR_IMMUTABLE in CvarInit().
  - Is there a mechanism to list available cvar/command names for autocomplete or console UI, or just cmdlist/cvarlist commands?

nodes.title: [build-deps] Build system & dependencies
nodes.description:
PURPOSE: OpenSoldat is a 2D multiplayer action game written in FreePascal that uses CMake as its primary build orchestrator. The build system compiles both a client (graphical) and dedicated server from shared Pascal sources, with support for multiple platforms (Windows, Linux, macOS) and cross-compilation. It manages complex native library dependencies (SDL2, OpenAL, FreeType, PhysFS, GameNetworkingSockets) and asset downloading.

CLIENT/SERVER: Client and server are built from the same codebase: both link shared/ (52 .pas core game logic), 3rdparty/ (SDL2 headers, PascalScript), but diverge at top level: client compiles client/*.pas (21 files) + client/libs (dglOpenGL, FreeType, openal, stb) + links SDL2 fully; server compiles server/*.pas (40 files) + server/scriptcore (game scripting) + links PhysFS only. CMake controls via BUILD_CLIENT and BUILD_SERVER options. Client is authority on rendering (OpenGL, graphics state), sound (OpenAL), input. Server is authority on game state, physics, scriptcore execution. Both use Net.pas (core protocol) + BitStream.pas serialization. Authority/prediction: shared mechanics (Sprites, Bullets, Control) run on both sides; clients interpolate, server validates.

KEY TYPES: CMake Build Configuration = Multi-stage build process: (1) CMake detects FreePascal >= 3.0, finds SDL2/OpenAL/FreeType/PhysFS, (2) optionally downloads GameNetworkingSockets v1.4.0 or assets, (3) compiles two executables (soldat client, soldatserver) from shared Pascal sources; TBitReader / TBitWriter = Network serialization classes in shared/libs/BitStream.pas: compact bitstream codec for game protocol (int8/16/32, floats, strings, booleans); PhysFS Virtual Filesystem = C library wrapper for mounting archives (.smod files) as directory trees; enables asset/mod loading from zips; GameNetworkingSockets = Valve's networking library v1.4.0: provides UDP transport, reliability, encryption for multiplayer (replaces older networking when not using Steam); Lazarus IDE Project Files = soldat.lpi / soldatserver.lpi: IDE metadata including unit paths, compiler options, project structure (not used in CMake builds but alternative build path); PascalScript ScriptCore = Server-side game scripting interpreter; ~50 source files in server/scriptcore define custom game rules engine; Asset Manifest = soldat.smod (game data archive) + play-regular.ttf downloaded from GitHub opensoldat/base repository v0.2, SHA1 verified

RESPONSIBILITIES: Detect FreePascal 3.0+ compiler and configure unit search paths (-Fu flags) for shared, client, server, 3rdparty directories; Find and link native libraries: SDL2 (windowing/input), OpenAL (audio), FreeType (fonts), PhysFS (archives), GameNetworkingSockets (networking); Download and verify game assets: soldat.smod and play-regular.ttf from GitHub releases with SHA1 checksums; Manage platform-specific library linking: SDL2 as framework on macOS, dll/so on Windows/Linux; handle OpenGL linking (-framework OpenGL on macOS); Configure RPATH/install_name_dir for dynamic library discovery at runtime (esp. macOS @executable_path and Linux $ORIGIN); Build two independent executables: soldat (client, 21 .pas files) and soldatserver (server, 40 .pas files) from 52 shared .pas files; Support optional features: BUILD_STEAM (Link steam_api instead of GNS), BUILD_SCRIPTCORE (Server scripting), ADD_ASSETS (automatic asset download); Enable cross-compilation to 6 target platforms: Windows/Linux/macOS x86_64 and x86_32 via CROSS_* CMake options; Configure compiler flags: Debug (-O1 -g -gl -dDEVELOPMENT) vs Release (-O3 -CX -XX -dTESTING), with warnings suppression (-vm flags); Build sub-libraries: stb (SHARED C library for image processing) with platform-specific compilation; Manage install step: clean binaries, copy to CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, preserve .smod and .dll/.so/.dylib files, set proper permissions

DATA FLOW: Configure-time: (1) CMake detects environment (OS, FPC version, library paths from pkg-config or manual VCPKG), (2) downloads assets via FetchContent if ADD_ASSETS=ON, (3) generates FPC compiler flags and unit include paths. Build-time: (1) CMake invokes FPC compiler on soldat.lpr and soldatserver.lpr, (2) FPC resolves unit dependencies (GLOB_RECURSE sources), (3) links C libraries via -k flags and custom targets (stb, GameNetworkingSockets, external SDL2/OpenAL/FreeType/PhysFS), (4) outputs bin/soldat and bin/soldatserver executables, (5) copies assets to bin/ folder. Install-time: (1) copies binaries and libraries to CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, (2) sets RPATH for runtime library discovery, (3) excludes temporary files, config dirs, logs.

INTERNAL DEPS: cmake_modules/ utilities (utils.cmake, SoldatAssets.cmake, CMakeDeterminePascalInformation.cmake, CMakeDeterminePascalCompiler.cmake, FindSDL2.cmake); 3rdparty/Pascal-SDL-2-Headers (SDL2 bindings, 50+ .pas/.inc files); 3rdparty/pascalscript (embedded PascalScript interpreter, 50+ .pas files); shared/ (52 .pas files: AI, Anims, Game, Weapons, PolyMap, Cvar, etc.); shared/libs (BitStream.pas for network serialization, PhysFS/SteamWrapper/KrakenSDK bindings); shared/mechanics/ (5 .pas files: Bullets, Control, Sparks, Sprites, Things); shared/network/ (20 .pas files: Net.pas core, NetworkClient*, NetworkServer*, FAE/attestation support); client/libs/ (dglOpenGL, FreeType, openal, stb Pascal bindings and C code); server/scriptcore/ (33 subdirectories, game rule scripting engine)

EXTERNAL DEPS: SDL2 (windowing, input, rendering context on all platforms), OpenAL (audio playback), OpenGL (graphics rendering via dglOpenGL bindings), FreeType (font rasterization), PhysFS (virtual filesystem, archive mounting), GameNetworkingSockets v1.4.0 (networking library from Valve, uses protobuf internally), protobuf (protocol buffers for GameNetworkingSockets), OpenSSL (encryption for GNS), Steam SDK (optional, links steam_api64.dll/libsteam_api.so/libsteam_api.dylib if BUILD_STEAM=ON), FreePascal 3.0+ (compiler and RTL), CMake 3.14+ (build orchestration)

MODERNIZATION RISKS: 
  - Pascal-to-modern-language migration: 169 .pas files + 50 PascalScript files; Pascal OOP is single-inheritance, no templates, uses interfaces; lots of legacy patterns (pointer arithmetic, manual memory management in BitStream, global state in Cvar.pas)
  - CMAKE_Pascal_FLAGS and FPC compiler invocation: custom CMake language detection module is non-standard; cross-compilation flags (-Twin64, -Px86_64) are FPC-specific, not portable
  - Lazarus IDE project files (.lpi) hardcoded paths and IDE metadata; must manually replicate compiler flags if moving away from CMake/FPC
  - Tight coupling: shared/libs/BitStream.pas has pointer arithmetic (FBuffers: TFPGList<PByte>); shared/libs/PhysFS.pas assumes dll/so naming; client/libs all assume C FFI which requires FPC
  - Asset downloading: SoldatAssets.cmake uses SHA1 verification (deprecated, should be SHA256); GitHub releases as single source of truth
  - Global state: Cvar.pas (48KB) is likely a large singleton registry of config variables; Game.pas (24KB), Weapons.pas (44KB) likely hold global game state
  - PascalScript embedding: server/scriptcore tightly couples PascalScript interpreter API; custom FFI layer in scriptcore/ may break on version change
  - Platform-specific code: Darwin framework linking (-framework OpenGL, -framework OpenAL) hardcoded; Windows PE security flags embedded in .lpr; Linux RPATH $ORIGIN assumes relative layout
  - Version pinning: FreePascal 3.0.4, SDL 2.0.12, FreeType 2.6.1, PhysFS 3.0.2, GNS v1.4.0 all hardcoded; update risks breaking ABI compatibility

OPEN QUESTIONS: 
  - How does the shared code distinguish between client and server compile-time vs runtime? Are there -dSERVER / -dCLIENT conditionals in shared/*.pas?
  - What does KrakenSDK (Fae/NanoKraken) do? It's in shared/libs but not referenced in CMakeLists; is it dead code or conditional feature?
  - How does PascalScript ScriptCore FFI work? What's the contract between native game code (Sprites, Bullets) and script-defined rules?
  - Is stb.c source included or pre-compiled? CMakeLists.txt says 'add_library(stb SHARED src/stb.c)' but what's in src/?
  - Asset hash verification: soldat.smod uses SHA1 (security issue), why not SHA256? Is there a reason to keep old hash?
  - GameNetworkingSockets: does the build assume OpenSSL headers are available? How is protobuf dependency resolved on Windows (vcpkg) vs Linux (apt) vs macOS (brew)?
  - Cross-compilation: are there pre-built library artifacts for CROSS_WINDOWS_64 targets, or does the build expect vcpkg/system libraries for target platform?
  - macOS frameworks: why hardcoded -framework OpenGL / -framework OpenAL instead of using CMake's find_package results?
  - RPATH on macOS: CMAKE_INSTALL_NAME_DIR is @executable_path/../Frameworks but target_library_install_dir is also ../Frameworks—is the double relative path intentional?
  - Lazarus IDE: are .lpi files kept in sync with CMakeLists.txt manually, or is there a tool to sync them? What happens if IDE config drifts?

nodes.title: Decision: TypeScript, web-first, clean-break protocol, faithful-first port
nodes.description:
User-selected stack across 4 axes:
1) LANGUAGE: TypeScript (strict). One language for sim/client/server/mods.
2) NET/DATA: Clean-break versioned protocol (protobuf-es over WebTransport). New server/client population; legacy demos dropped; frees us from scrambled TGun/Keys16/wire caps.
3) STRATEGY: Faithful-first then refactor. Phase A mirrors Pascal globals (1-indexed, sentinel-0) and ports the Parts.pas integrator ~line-by-line, gated by a golden-master determinism test; clean architecture/ECS deferred to Phase C.
4) DISTRIBUTION: Web-first. Renderer WebGL2/WebGPU (PixiJS v8), audio WebAudio, transport WebTransport. Native (Tauri) later.

KEY TECHNICAL CRUX: Pascal physics uses Single (f32); JS is f64. Resolution: clean-break means both TS sides share f64 so internal determinism is free; f32-fidelity needed ONLY to validate feel via golden master + a STRICT_F32 (Math.fround) dev flag. Plan: docs/PORT-PLAN.md.

Committed on rewrite/ts-port (6fe83cd, 0882109).

nodes.title: STRICT_F32 divergence watch-items for M2 golden master
nodes.description: Porters flagged two fidelity risks to validate against a Pascal trace at M2: (1) vec2.dot wraps each multiply AND the add in f(), but Pascal Vec2Dot is a single unrounded Single expression x1*x2 + y1*y2 — the physics agent inlined dot/length in satisfyConstraintsFor to match per-op rounding; if golden master diverges, drop the inner f() on the dot sum to match Pascal fused expr. (2) Doc discrepancy: wire-protocol.md said ORIGINAL_WEAPONS=64 but source Weapons.pas:86 is 20 (corrected in protocol).

nodes.title: [review] f32-wrap discipline has no enforcement yet
nodes.description: Oversight finding (M2 risk). scalar.ts ships f = STRICT_F32 ? Math.fround : identity, but the plan's promised lint/codegen rule that forces every arithmetic step in the integrator to be f()-wrapped does NOT exist. f32-exact reproduction depends on a human remembering to wrap every op. When the golden master diverges at tick N, locating which of ~200 unwrapped ops caused it is extremely costly. Recommendation: build the enforcement (eslint rule or a typed Scalar wrapper that makes unwrapped arithmetic a type error) BEFORE porting ParticleSystem, not after.

nodes.title: [review] Pascal Single fidelity may over-promise bit-exactness
nodes.description: Oversight finding (M2 risk). Math.fround(a+b) does not generally equal Pascal Single semantics: Pascal rounds to Single at each store to a Single var; JS keeps the full f64 intermediate within an expression. Matching requires wrapping precisely where FPC materializes a Single temp, which depends on FPC expression evaluation. Plan says 'start epsilon=0'; scalar.ts already carries EPSILON=1e-4. Treat epsilon=0 as aspirational per-function, expect a small per-function/per-window epsilon, and have the golden master REPORT first-divergence function rather than assert global bit-equality.

nodes.title: [review] Golden master depends on building+instrumenting original Pascal
nodes.description: Oversight finding (M2 blocker risk, not in risk register). The {$IFDEF GOLDENMASTER} trace dump needs a working FPC/Lazarus build of OpenSoldat. If that toolchain is not stood up, M2 stalls regardless of TS quality. Verify 'can we build and instrument the original at all?' on day one, BEFORE writing TS physics.

nodes.title: [review] M0 acceptance says 'CI passes' but no CI exists for soldat-ts
nodes.description: Oversight finding (M0). The only GH workflows present are decision-graph/pages deploys. M0 is not done until typecheck+test+lint run green in CI. Land CI inside M0 rather than slipping it to 'later'.

nodes.description: Oversight finding (sequencing). The project thesis is 'retire the riskiest unknown first', yet M1 (map rendering) is low-risk, visually rewarding, and a classic schedule sink, and is numbered before M2. The 'first two weeks' list does interleave M2 work (tasks 6-8) which is good, but watch that map-render polish does not crowd out the golden-master spike.

nodes.description: Golden-master harness (ScenarioRunner/GoldenTrace/compareTraces) validates free-fall closed form over 600 ticks + internal determinism + perturbation detection, green in f64 AND STRICT_F32. Sprites.pas movement core ported (control->forces, SURFACECOEF friction, on-ground latch, MAX_VELOCITY clamp, tick order); minimal floor collision (full PolyMap deferred to M3). Pascal instrumentation patch under tools/golden-master (capture needs fpc). 104 tests total. Commit 044b821.

nodes.title: [review] M0 marked done but no TS CI gate exists (updates #46)
nodes.description: Delta review #2. CI status of finding 46 is NOT resolved. .github/workflows/soldat.yml is the ORIGINAL OpenSoldat FreePascal pipeline (cmake/make on Linux/Win/macOS); it runs no pnpm/tsc/vitest job for soldat-ts. PROCESS.md marks M0 done on the basis of '104 tests pass locally' + 'tsc --build clean', but M0's stated acceptance is 'CI passes'. Gap: nothing in CI gates the TS port, and STRICT_F32=1 vitest is never run on a runner. Recommend a small soldat-ts job (pnpm i, tsc --build, vitest run, STRICT_F32=1 vitest run) before treating M0 as truly closed.

nodes.title: [review] Opportunity: legacy CI already provisions fpc — run the deferred Pascal golden trace in CI
nodes.description: Delta review #2, constructive. Node 50 deferred the Pascal-side golden-master TRACE CAPTURE because no fpc is available locally. But soldat.yml installs fpc on the ubuntu and macos runners already. The instrument-serverloop.patch + trace-format.md are written and ready. So the fidelity cross-check that finding 45 flagged could be AUTOMATED in CI: apply the patch, build instrumented soldat, capture a fixed-seed bot trace, run it as a golden fixture against @soldat/sim under STRICT_F32. That converts M2's 'fpc trace cross-check pending' from a manual someday-task into a CI gate, and is the cleanest way to actually retire finding 45.

nodes.title: M3 progress: PolyMap collision + real .PMS in client
nodes.description: PolyMap sector collision system ported (PointInPoly, sector grid, ClosestPerpendicular, collideCircle, POLY_TYPE_* helpers) + buildPolyMap from .PMS. Faithful collision-resolution primitive resolveParticleMapCollision (Sprites.pas:2718-2751: perp pushout clamped to |v|, bouncy reflect) integrated into sprite movement via collideSpriteAgainstMap. Client now loads real .PMS with synthetic fallback. 115 tests green f64+STRICT_F32. Commits 34f74bd, d562684.

nodes.title: M3 remaining: multi-point foot collision + Area gating
nodes.description: collideSpriteAgainstMap currently queries the COM particle as a stand-in. Faithful Soldat CheckMapCollision tests multiple skeleton FOOT points and applies Area/animation gating (Sprites.pas:2731-2772) to decide whether to resolve and to snap-to-rest (Pos:=OldPos; Forces.Y-=GRAV). Porting the multi-point loop + animation/LegsAnimation state is the next M3 step before standing/walking on real geometry feels correct. Also still pending: jump/jetpack impulses and the golden-master fpc cross-check.

nodes.title: [review] RNG is not Pascal-bit-compatible — caps golden-master scope for combat/bots
nodes.description: Delta review #3. New file rng.ts is mulberry32 and (per its own docstring) NOT bit-compatible with FreePascal Random. Two layers of divergence from Pascal: (1) the underlying stream differs (FPC 3.x Random is a Mersenne Twister MT19937), and (2) nextInt uses floor(next()*n) whereas FPC Random(L) uses a multiply-shift: longint((qword(genrand)*qword(L)) shr 32). Consequence: any golden-master scenario touching bullet spread, spark jitter, bot decisions, or the wire bullet seed CANNOT reproduce a Pascal trace until both the MT19937 stream and the Random(n) mapping are ported exactly. Mitigation today is correct (golden scenarios are RNG-free free-fall), but M4 combat fidelity is ungateable until this lands. Recommend porting FPC MT19937 + multiply-shift mapping before/with the first RNG-dependent golden scenario.

nodes.title: [review] M3/M4 are accumulating on an unproven M2 fpc-fidelity gate (blast-radius risk)
nodes.description: Delta review #3. M3 (PolyMap collision) landed and M4 (bullets/weapons/sparks/damage) has begun, yet the M2 golden-master Pascal cross-check is still pending (no fpc trace captured; current validation is closed-form free-fall only — finding 45). Building combat on top of an integrator whose Soldat-fidelity is unverified means a later fpc-trace divergence would have an M2+M3+M4 blast radius rather than M2. Mitigant: ports carry verbatim PORT: file:line comments so re-validation is mechanical, and combat is largely additive. Recommendation: prioritize wiring the already-written instrument-serverloop.patch through the fpc-provisioned CI (finding 52) NOW, before M4 grows further, so the feel core is locked before more code depends on it.

nodes.title: [review] 6 milestones done, 0 fidelity gates fired — insert a reconciliation gate BEFORE M6 netcode
nodes.description: Delta review #4. M4 (node 57) and M5 (node 59) now both 'done', making M0-M5 complete in one session. But a systemic deferral pattern spans every gameplay milestone: M3 foot collision (node 54), M4 bullet hitbox + ricochet/AoE + Pascal RNG (node 58), M5 bot LOS/weapon-model (node 60) all use COM-particle/single-circle/16-sample stand-ins, and the Pascal fidelity gate (fpc golden trace + MT19937 RNG sequence) remains deferred at every step. Net: six milestones marked done with ZERO golden-master fidelity gate having actually fired — 'done' currently means 'structurally complete with documented shortcuts', not 'faithful'. The shortcuts are individually reasonable and well-tracked (nodes 54/58/60), and step.ts faithfully ports the ServerLoop UpdateFrame tick order — so structure is sound. The risk is timing: M6 is netcode. Building the clean-break protocol, demo format, and client prediction against an unvalidated feel core risks baking divergence into the wire/demo contract, where it is far more expensive to unwind post-net. Recommendation: insert an explicit fidelity-reconciliation gate before M6 — capture one fpc golden trace via the already-written instrument-serverloop.patch through the fpc-provisioned CI (finding 52), port MT19937+multiply-shift RNG (finding 55), and require the golden master to actually pass once before netcode hardens the contract.

nodes.title: M6 progress: protocol codec + replication + client prediction

nodes.title: [review] Verification depth: 7 milestones green by typecheck+unit-test, zero ground-truth validation
nodes.description: Delta review #5. M6 (codec/replication/prediction, node 64) and a 'playable SP' build (node 66) landed; M7 is 'launching' per PROCESS.md. node 67 states plainly: the client has NEVER been run in a real browser ('verified by typecheck only — no GPU smoke-test'), and sprite feel has NEVER been validated against a Pascal golden trace (closed-form only). So across M0-M6 + playable-SP, every milestone is 'done' on the strength of tsc --build + Vitest unit tests alone — validated entirely against the port's own internal assumptions, never against (a) a real browser runtime or (b) the original game's behavior. The two ground-truth checks that would catch a whole class of errors unit tests cannot (does it actually render/run? does it actually match Soldat?) are both perpetually deferred while feature milestones advance into netcode and now M7. Mitigant: the versioned clean-break codec means the wire contract can still evolve cheaply (softens finding 63). Recommendation: before M7 broadens surface area, force the two ground-truth gates ONCE — a browser smoke-test of the playable-SP loop, and a single fpc golden-trace cross-check — so the stack has been validated against reality at least once, not only against itself.

nodes.title: M8 done: mod API + sandboxed ScriptHost
nodes.description: New @soldat/modding: events.ts (28 events incl. OnPlayerDamage cascade), api.ts (ScriptGame/Player/Players/Map + createScriptApi over live World), host.ts ScriptHost (registration-order dispatch, cascade threading). KEY FIX vs PascalScript: per-handler try/catch so a crashing/hung mod is logged+skipped, never stalls the server (original escalated to shutdown after 10 errors); setHandlerInvoker is the isolated-vm/Worker+CPU-budget seam. Reconciled to ONE canonical contract (host imports api/events). 269 tests green f64+STRICT_F32. Commits 0fa755f, 4ce1ec8. This completes the numbered milestone arc M0-M8.
